commits.pr_title: [Deprecation] Deprecate `cudagraph_copy_inputs` and remove the compiler-managed input copy
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Deprecates `CompilationConfig.cudagraph_copy_inputs` as a no-op and removes the compiler-managed input copy behind it (`make_copy_and_call` and the `sym_tensor_indices` plumbing in the AOT cache).

## Claims

- No runner has ever enabled the flag: it was added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10203 for V1, but the model runners pass persistent input buffers to CUDA graphs themselves, so it only added a copy kernel per compiled call.
- Setting it now logs a deprecation warning (removal in v0.37.0) instead of failing config validation, and it is excluded from the compile factors.
- Supersedes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68485, which fixes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/68431 by extending the copy to non-leading token dims; with the copy gone, that crash cannot happen.

## Validation

`test_simple.py` passed fresh tensors on each call and relied on the copy; it now slices one persistent buffer, as it did before https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/10203. The gemma-3n test just drops the flag.

```
pytest tests/compile/fullgraph/test_simple.py -v
pytest tests/v1/e2e/general/test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill.py -v
```

On B200, commit 835853375f:

```
test_simple.py:                  5 passed, 17 warnings in 86.75s (0:01:26)
test_kv_sharing_fast_prefill.py: 3 passed, 3 warnings in 390.34s (0:06:30)
```

commits.pr_title: [Model] Remove DBRX
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove the native DBRX implementation (`DbrxForCausalLM`). `databricks/dbrx-instruct` and `databricks/dbrx-base` were deleted from the Hub long ago, so the model has been untested in CI (`is_available_online=False`) ever since. Open PRs https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49336 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49362 fix DBRX weight loading, so it has likely been broken on main too. This PR removes the model instead, so it does not duplicate them.

## Claims

- Deletes `vllm/model_executor/models/dbrx.py`, its registry and docs entries, `DbrxModelArchConfigConvertor`, the DBRX test entries (registry, pipeline parallel, arch config groundtruth) and the DBRX branches in the MoE kernel benchmarks.
- Adds `"DbrxForCausalLM": "0.34.0"` to `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS`.

## Validation

Commit `47bb58a9b7`, macOS CPU:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/config/test_model_arch_config.py tests/quantization/test_auto_gptq.py -q
# 73 passed, 1 skipped, 15 warnings in 44.65s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k test_hf_registry_coverage -q
# 1 passed, 474 deselected, 14 warnings in 0.83s
```

## Details

- Transformers has its own `DbrxForCausalLM`, so with `model_impl="auto"` a DBRX config now resolves to `TransformersForCausalLM` (checked with `ModelConfig` on a local `config.json`). That path is not validated because no checkpoint is available. The `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS` entry only fires if that fallback fails.
- The GPTQ "experts' parent prefix" handling in `gptq_utils.py` was written with DBRX in mind but is generic, so it stays. Only the DBRX wording in its comments changes.
- `tiktoken` stays in `requirements/common.txt` (Kimi-Audio uses it). Only its comment changes.

## TODO

Closed, since they only concern the removed DBRX implementation:

- [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/49004
- [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49336
- [x] https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49362

commits.pr_title: [RL][Weight Transfer] Add sparse_disk backend for sparse deltas through storage
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds `sparse_disk`, a weight transfer backend for sparse weight deltas published through storage, for trainers that cannot share an NCCL group with inference or that feed many replicas. The trainer publishes each version's patches as one file. Every inference worker keeps its part of the checkpoint in host memory, laid out as its load plan writes it. In an update, the worker applies the new files to that copy and copies its whole part into the model, so every update is a full direct reload through the load plan, with post-load processing rerun.

## Claims

- Sparse updates without an NCCL group between trainer and inference; every replica reads the same patch files.
- No new loading pattern: each update is a full direct reload, as dense NCCL with `use_load_plan` does. After `start_reload`, planned tensors are copied to the load plan's destinations and marked loaded, the names the plan leaves out go through `model.load_weights()`, and `finish_reload` reruns post-load processing. Configurations no load plan supports are refused at init; a model whose loads cannot be planned fails at the first update, which is sent before serving. Tested on a BF16 and a block-FP8 checkpoint (below).
- Pause on Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP4, H20:
  - 0.65–0.66 s to reload a version;
  - 0.90–1.73 / 1.47–1.77 / 2.98–3.48 s with 0.1 / 1 / 3 % of elements changed.

  For comparison, on the same node: 2.0–2.4 s for sparse NCCL and 0.74–0.90 s for dense NCCL with a load plan. Dense NCCL ran with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95`; at the default, its 1 GiB receive buffer did not fit.
- Each worker validates a patch file before writing that file's changes to its host copy. Restarted servers rebuild their copy from the startup checkpoint and replay the published files.
- A new engine file, its registration and docs; no core files change.

## Validation

Unit tests (CPU, on 8bd378f2b6):

    pytest tests/distributed/test_weight_transfer.py -k sparse_disk
    6 passed, 168 deselected, 1 warning in 1.22s

The six tests run on CPU; in CI they are in the optional nightly H100 Distributed Features job. CI does not exercise GPU mapping, pinned transfers, real tensor-parallel layouts or block FP8 (the last two need checkpoints it doesn't have); the H20 runs below did.

- `test_sparse_disk_updates_equal_a_cold_start_on_the_patched_checkpoint_cpu`: the model ends bit for bit equal to a cold start on the densely patched checkpoint in each of these cases:
  - after the trainer's sends;
  - on a reload after the weights were lost;
  - on a restarted server that replays the files;
  - on a server started from a newer checkpoint, with the file it already contains deleted.

  It also checks that a re-init with another `base_version`, an update older than the model (also after a rebuild that stopped partway), and a second publish of a version are refused.

  The toy model covers tensor-parallel halves along both dims, a tensor split over two parameters, a 0-dim tensor, a name the load plan leaves to `load_weights` (its loader changes its input in place), a name the model skips, three dtypes, and patches cut across chunks.
- `test_sparse_disk_bad_file_is_refused_before_any_write_cpu`: a file with one bad patch is refused before it writes the host copy, and a new update to the last version restores the model. The bad patch has an unknown name, a wrong shape or dtype, an index repeated across a chunk boundary, or an out-of-range index.

The two follow-up commits, ea337843fb and 8bd378f2b6, add refusals and version checks, clean up a failed publish, check patch names against the tensors the default loader yields, and trim the code. They do not change how a file is mapped, written or loaded, so the end-to-end runs below still apply.

End to end on 8×H20 in one node, with a concurrency-32 completion load running. Each pause is measured from `/pause` to `/resume`. Patch files were written on the same node before each pause and read from the page cache; a file not yet on the host adds its read time to the pause. The H20 runs used a wheel built from main at `dd8c157895`, with the tested weight-transfer files overlaid.

<details>
<summary>Server commands</summary>

    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 vllm serve Qwen3-30B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 4 --moe-backend triton \
        --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_disk"}'

    # this environment's FlashInfer build lacks a header for its block-FP8 GEMM
    VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1 VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0 vllm serve Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
        --tensor-parallel-size 8 --weight-transfer-config '{"backend": "sparse_disk"}'

</details>

| Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16, TP4, 9 versions | pause |
|---|---|
| first update (load plan + host copy, 14.24 GiB pinned per worker) | 14.0 s |
| reload only | 0.65–0.66 s |
| 0.1 % | 0.90–1.73 s |
| 1 % | 1.47–1.77 s |
| 3 % | 2.98–3.48 s |
| restarted server, replay of 9 versions | 23.6 s |

After all 9 versions, the weights equal those from sparse NCCL and from dense NCCL on the same patches, by the `/weight_checker` digest over every parameter, and probe completions are bit for bit equal. The restarted server ends on the same weights. There were no client errors in 8480 requests, and a file with an out-of-range index, written past the writer's checks, was refused.

| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8, TP8, 3 versions | pause |
|---|---|
| first update (load plan + 46.75 GiB pinned host copy per worker) | 112.6 s |
| reload only | 3.31 s |
| 0.1 % / 1 % of the patched shards | 3.44–4.28 / 3.70 s |

The patches change 3 of the 94 checkpoint shards, including the model's 45 GDN `conv1d` weights, which the load plan leaves to `load_weights`. After 3 versions, the weights equal a cold start from the checkpoint with every patch applied. Probes are bit for bit equal, with no client errors.

These runs used the engine from one cleanup before the first commit, 1be69b3d90 (argument passing, a copy for fallback names, skipping names without a box in a slot, blocking copies where the dtype converts, refusing non-integer counts). On that commit's engine, the BF16 checks passed again on a second 8×H20 node, against sparse NCCL there, which ended on the same digest as on the first node. Steady-state pauses there were up to about 20 % longer; the first update took 41.4 s instead of 14.0 s, and the replay after a restart 51.0 s instead of 23.6 s. A later run on the first node took 100.2 s for the first update, probably with the checkpoint evicted from the page cache (not verified). The FP8 run was not repeated. Each figure is from one run, not repeated measurements.

## Details

- **Host copy.** The first update builds the load plan from the tensors the default loader yields. It then copies every box this worker loads into one host buffer per checkpoint dtype, pinned at its exact size. A name the plan leaves to `load_weights` keeps its whole tensor there. That is about the checkpoint size divided by TP per worker: 14.24 GiB for the 30B model at TP4.
- **Patch files.** For each values dtype, a file holds one concatenated index tensor (int32 unless a tensor has more than 2^31 elements) and one value tensor. The metadata records each tensor's name, shape and count, plus a format marker. Indices are strictly increasing per tensor, and a tensor appears at most once per version. The writer and every worker check both. A failed write tries to remove the file it created.
- **Apply.** Each worker checks the file's metadata, then checks every element and maps it to its offset in the copy, on its device, in chunks sized to its free memory, at least 2^20 elements. Only then does it write the copy. A failure before the write leaves the copy as it was. A failed write discards the copy, and the next update rebuilds it. Names the plan leaves to `load_weights` get a copy of their tensor, so a loader that changes its input cannot change the host copy.
- **Why not reload checkpoint files.** On the same setup, reloading the whole model took:
  - 7.2 s from a page-cached copy of the checkpoint files with the default loader;
  - 5.7–5.9 s from the same files with the load plan;
  - 2.4–3.8 s from pageable host memory;
  - 0.65 s from pinned memory.

  So the copy lives in pinned memory, not in files.
- **Versions.** A server follows versions forward from the `base_version` of its first init; a re-init with another base, or an update older than the model, is refused.
- **Not a duplicate.** An earlier open PR uses the same backend name for a different design: it reads one patch file inside each update and applies it in place, with no versions and no host copy. This PR versions the files, keeps a host copy per worker and reloads through the load plan. No code is shared. ModelExpress, already in tree, also replays deltas from object storage, through its own service; this backend needs only a shared directory.
- **Limitations.**
  - Needs the default loader (not `fastsafetensors` or `instanttensor`) and a load plan: direct reload, no EPLB, no online quantization, no secondary weight sources.
  - Draft weights are not updated.
  - Takes host memory on every server, plus about 10 bytes per changed element on each worker while a version applies.
  - Nothing checks that the patch files match the base checkpoint.
  - A failed update leaves the model mid-update; keep generation paused until an update succeeds. On TP>1 that currently needs a server restart, because later requests get the failed one's error.
  - Tested on Hopper (H20) only; SM100 was not tested. Timings there will differ: the copy goes over a different host link and post-load processing is heavier. The engine has no architecture-specific code.
- **Size.** About 440 code lines in the engine file, for the host copy, its index tables and the chunked device mapping. On the H20 BF16 TP4 run, a reload alone went from 6.3–6.9 s to 0.65–0.66 s, and an update with 0.1–3 % changed from 29.7–37.3 s to 0.90–3.48 s. The earlier figures are from a previous version of this PR, which reloaded from a file copy of the checkpoint.

Usage, recovery and limits are documented in `docs/training/weight_updates/engines/sparse_disk.md`.

## Credit

@AravindKurapati is a co-author of this change: his earlier #61083 proposed the same `sparse_disk` backend. The squash commit was merged before his `Co-authored-by` trailer was added, so this note records it.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Kimi-K3] Composite transparent images over the checkpoint background
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Kimi-K3 / K3.1 images with transparency (RGBA, LA, palette with a transparent colour) are preprocessed differently from the checkpoint's own image processor. vLLM drops the alpha channel; the checkpoint blends the image over an 8 px chessboard. This is a regression from #59278, which moved K3 to `KimiK25FusedVisionProcessor`.

## Claims

- For Kimi-K3, transparent images now give the same pixels as the checkpoint's image processor.
- RGB images and Kimi-K2.5 are unchanged.

## Validation

One commit, `61d19e1b654eaad2b68faa1a5c82b8e3888cc0c9`, on main `ab1c06419cf62eb8cfed2e61548dbb92b92f7ca4`. Everything below ran on CPU only, with compiled extensions taken from a main build at `8c17e4692a`.

New test, failing before and passing after:

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py -q \
  --deselect tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py::test_mm_device_do_normalize

# main ab1c06419c with the new test: 4 failed, 6 passed, 1 deselected in 6.15s
#   FAILED test_fused_image_processor_composites_transparency_like_hf[RGBA-310-470]
#   FAILED test_fused_image_processor_composites_transparency_like_hf[RGBA-7300-30]
#   FAILED test_fused_image_processor_composites_transparency_like_hf[LA-310-470]
#   FAILED test_fused_image_processor_composites_transparency_like_hf[P-310-470]
#   e.g. AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!
#        Mismatched elements: 424224 / 479808 (88.4%)
#        Greatest absolute difference: 2.0
# this PR: 10 passed, 1 deselected in 5.79s
```

Neighbouring suites with this PR:

```
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py tests/multimodal/media/test_image.py \
  tests/renderers/test_kimi_k3.py -q \
  --deselect tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_kimi_k3.py::test_mm_device_do_normalize
# 66 passed, 86 skipped, 1 deselected in 24.64s

pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -q -k "Kimi-K3"    # 3 passed, 3 skipped (Kimi-K3.1 not in the local cache)
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -q -k "Kimi-K2.5"  # 3 passed
```

`pre-commit run --files` on the two changed files: all hooks pass.

<details>
<summary>More checks (CPU, ad hoc scripts, not part of the PR)</summary>

Chat path: `renderer.render_chat` with a PNG data URL. Largest absolute difference of the rendered `pixel_values` (after applying the checkpoint's mean/std) against the checkpoint's `AutoImageProcessor` on the same PNG:

| Image | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| RGB 310x470 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
| RGBA 310x470 | 2.0 | 0.0 |
| RGBA 7300x30 (resized) | 2.0 | 0.0 |
| LA 310x470 | 1.93 | 0.0 |
| P with transparency 310x470 | 2.0 | 0.0 |

Processor level, 27 synthetic images per model: 9 modes (RGB, RGBA, LA, P with transparency, P, L, CMYK, 1, I;16) x 3 sizes (310x470, 7300x30, 13x9).

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| Kimi-K3, exact match with the checkpoint's processor | main 15/27, this PR 27/27 |
| Kimi-K2.5, output byte-identical to main | 27/27, plus a 4-frame RGBA `video_chunk` |

Besides the transparent modes, the Kimi-K3 mismatches on main include the downscaled 7300x30 images in P, CMYK, 1 and I;16. The checkpoint resizes in the image's original mode and main converted to RGB first.

</details>

Not run:

- The tests and checks used the Kimi-K3 checkpoint files only. For Kimi-K3.1 Pro I only compared files: its `preprocessor_config.json` has the same two keys and its `media_utils.py` is identical.
- No GPU or served-model run of this branch. `test_mm_device_do_normalize` needs a GPU and was deselected.
- No model evaluation. I know of no benchmark that sends transparent images. For RGB input the changed code returns the image as before, see the RGB rows above.
- No test through `LLM` or a launched server. Pixel values are not observable there without loading the K3 weights, so the regression test compares the two processors directly. It runs in the CPU "Multimodal Processor" CI step.

## Details

Root cause: K3's `preprocessor_config.json` sets `transparent_bg_config` (a chessboard) and `transparent_bg_fill_stage: "after_resize"`. The K3 renderer loads images with `image_mode=None` so that alpha reaches the processor. The fused processor ignored both keys and called `image.convert("RGB")`.

Fix: the fused processor reads the two keys and mirrors `fill_transparent_bg_with` from the checkpoint's `media_utils.py`. It blends over the configured background, before or after the resize as configured. Kimi-K2.5 sets neither key and keeps the old path (convert to RGB before the resize).

Behaviour changes to be aware of:

- For K3 the resize now runs in the image's original mode, as the checkpoint does. This also changes downscaled palette, bilevel, CMYK and 16-bit images (see the details block).
- `KimiK25FusedVisionProcessor.resize_image` is now an instance method. It has no other caller in the tree.
- A `video_chunk` with RGBA frames given to the fused processor with the K3 config is now composited too. The checkpoint's K3 processor does not accept video chunks, so there is no reference for this.
- The solid backgrounds (`white`, `black`, `gray`) are implemented from the reference code but not covered by a test, since no checkpoint config uses them.
- Python frontend only. I did not look at the Rust frontend's K3 path.

Not a duplicate: searches of open PRs and issues for `transparent_bg_config`, `kimi_k25_vision_fused`, "Kimi-K3 transparent", "Kimi RGBA" and "Kimi chessboard" found no PR or issue for this. #63912 (merged) is about the Rust frontend's default white background. Related open PRs:

- #69584 (K3 image and text order) changes a different source file and the same test file. A trial merge with this branch is clean.
- #58538 (path checks in Kimi vision loading) edits `_to_pil` in the same file. A trial merge has one conflict hunk there; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.
- #66849 (draft, K3 video) already conflicts with main and also edits this file.
- #69256 (K3 video) merges cleanly with this branch.

No docs change: no flag, field or default is added.

AI assistance was used to write this change.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] GDS kv offloading support
commits.pr_body:
This is the second part of the implementation of RFC https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/54777. This part includes the GDS implementation on top of the KV offload fs support. ## Overview Implement GDS as a file system offloading connector. ## Claims GDS enables direct transfer from GPU to disk, enabling far faster kv cache access when the cache is on a file system. In our testing using inference-perf, we are seeing more than x2 throughput improvement when loading the kv cache from fs using GDS. The above graphs are from running inference-perf using Meta-Llama-3.1-8B and 8xH100 against a shared file system. To see the best performance you want to set VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=BLHNC and use one offloading connector (multi-tier with cpu and fs offloading) for write, and use the GDS connector for read. ## Validation Several new test units have been added under tests/v1/kv_offload/fs, including test_gds_worker.py ## Details Example of native kv_offloading using the multi-connector, multi-tiering, and GDS: --kv-transfer-config { "kv_connector": "MultiConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "connectors": [ { "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec", "cpu_bytes_to_use": 107374182400, "block_size": 256, "secondary_tiers": [ { "type": "fs", "access_mode": "write", "root_dir": "/mnt/files-storage", "n_read_threads": 32, "n_write_threads": 32 } ] } }, { "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector", "kv_role": "kv_both", "kv_connector_extra_config": { "spec_name": "GDSOffloadingSpec", "block_size":256, "access_mode": "read", "gds_root_dir": "/mnt/files-storage" } }]} } ---

commits.pr_title: [XPU][CI] Raise API Server Scale Out step timeout to 60 minutes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Raise `timeout_in_minutes` of the Intel GPU CI step `:intel: (BMG) Entrypoints Integration (API Server Scale Out)` from 40 to 60.

The step now times out on most `vllm/intel-ci` builds (e.g. 19387, 19399, 19415, 19420, 19427, 19429-19431, 19436, 19444, 19447, 19451, 19452, 19458, 19460). The tests themselves all pass: the job is killed by Buildkite (`signal: terminated`) while still running `test_serving_tokens.py`. `tests/entrypoints/scale_out` grew a lot this month (41 commits, about 3k added lines since 2026-11-01), and the suite now takes longer than the 40-minute budget. Passing retries already took 35-40 min of wall-clock time.

No single PR caused this. The time grew gradually across many scale-out test additions.

## Test Plan

Run the exact CI command in the CI image `public.ecr.aws/q9t5s3a7/vllm-ci-test-repo:7b7af30196ad3f12eadaa008fb3bf589ba02d520-xpu` on 1x Arc Pro B60:

```bash
export VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn && cd tests && pytest -v -s entrypoints/scale_out \
  --deselect="tests/entrypoints/scale_out/derender/test_derender_parity.py::test_inline_derender_parity[n2]" \
```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Cache] Fix Mamba decode resume caching a block that holds a later state
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Fixes #70066. After a preemption, `_decode_resume_block_idx` can keep a Mamba block that holds the state of a later position, and `cache_blocks_on_free` then caches it under its block-end hash. This checks `_mid_block_states` instead of `_checkpoints`, which async scheduling clears too early.

## Claims

- A block that holds a state other than its block end is no longer cached as a decode-resume state.
- Correct decode-resume hits are unchanged.

## Validation

Tested at 69d3af837 on an RTX 3050 Ti under WSL2. `single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` is unchanged at this PR's base. Both builds also carry the fix from #69991, because `prefix_match_unit` crashes on this machine without it.

The new test fails on main and passes with this PR. The sync case passes on both, because the old check holds there by timing:

```text
$ pytest -v tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_mamba_decode_resume_skips_off_boundary_checkpoint_block tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py::test_mamba_sparse_retention_caches_decode_resume_state_on_free

main:
test_mamba_decode_resume_skips_off_boundary_checkpoint_block[False] PASSED
test_mamba_decode_resume_skips_off_boundary_checkpoint_block[True] FAILED
test_mamba_sparse_retention_caches_decode_resume_state_on_free[0] PASSED
test_mamba_sparse_retention_caches_decode_resume_state_on_free[1] PASSED
E       assert 64 == 0
========================= 1 failed, 3 passed in 2.14s ==========================

this PR:
============================== 4 passed in 1.35s ===============================
```

The other core tests (`tests/v1/core/` prefix caching, KV cache manager and scheduler tests, and `tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_utils.py`) fail in the same places with and without the fix, apart from the new test. Those failures need `facebook/opt-125m`, which isn't cached on this offline machine. On a machine with network access (RTX 2000 Ada), `test_prefix_caching.py` and `test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` all pass with this PR (317 tests), and only the new test fails on main.

End to end, I used a hand-built Qwen3.5-style checkpoint whose output depends exactly on the state vLLM reads ([glassbox](https://github.com/sansblues/glassbox)), with block size 576 and `prefix_match_unit=64`. A clean step has a logit margin of about 39.7:

| Run | main | this PR | v0.34.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 request preempted at 858 and aborted; a second request reuses its first 1053 tokens | stale 576 hit, margin drops to 13.0 | no hit, 39.75 | no hit, 39.75 (one seed) |
| Same, without preemption (a correct hit) | 576 hit, 39.75 | 576 hit, 39.75 | |
| n=3 parallel sampling with 118–140 preemptions, 2 passes | 95/96 per pass, one wrong token | 96/96 | 96/96 |

On the real Qwen3.5-0.8B, the stale 576 hit shows up in `num_cached_tokens` and goes away with the fix, but the greedy tokens are the same either way.

## Details

`_decode_resume_block_idx` (from #67053) skips a block when `_checkpoints` says a resumed prefill left an off-boundary checkpoint in it. `_checkpoints` only describes the current step, though. With async scheduling, the next step is scheduled before the resumed prefill finishes, and that clears the entry, so the block is kept and later cached under its block-end hash.

`_mid_block_states` (from #67717) already tracks, for as long as the request holds its blocks, which blocks hold a state other than their block end, and `_refine_block_mask` uses it to keep them out of the full-block hash. Checking it here makes decode resume follow the same rule. For a request that was never preempted, it only lists blocks inside the prompt, which the function already skips, so nothing changes there.

The cost is that such a request caches no decode state until it crosses the next block end. The block-end state it would have cached was never computed, so nothing correct is lost.

The test drives a real `KVCacheManager` and mirrors the scheduler's order of steps by hand. There's no `LLM`-level test, because I couldn't make the bug change a real model's output.

I used Claude to find the bug and to write the fix and test. I reviewed every line and ran the checks above myself.

---

commits.pr_title: [Core][Perf] Deprioritize superseded Mamba prefix-cache states
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Deprioritize Mamba/GDN/PLE prefix-cache states that are two or more turns behind a conversation's latest cached tip (`t-2` and older), while keeping the immediate predecessor (`t-1`), shared system-prompt junctions, and multi-branch fork points in normal LRU.

Fully encapsulated in `MambaManager` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, plus a generic `reset_prefix_cache()` dispatch in `kv_cache_coordinator.py`), reusing the `FreeKVCacheBlockQueue._cached_head` middle eviction tier (`uncached -> deprioritized -> normal LRU cached`) and `BlockPool.deprioritize_blocks()` merged in #68820 with **no changes to `kv_cache_manager.py` or `block_pool.py`**.

Related PRs:
- Directly reuses `BlockPool.deprioritize_blocks()` from #68820 as-is.
- Differs materially from #63808 and #64975 in two ways (see **Details**): (1) evicts deprioritized blocks **after** uncached blocks rather than prepending ahead of uncached blocks, and (2) retains one immediate predecessor (`t-1`) and shared fork/system-prompt checkpoints in normal LRU rather than demoting `t-1` immediately (`k=0`), eliminating coding-agent tail-rollback regressions (up to **+41.7%** under fine-grained prefix hashing) while reducing recompute tokens by up to **13.7%** on real AgentX traces.

## Claims

- Encapsulated in `MambaManager` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`; zero changes to `kv_cache_manager.py` or `block_pool.py`, zero new classes/enums or `__init__` API changes):
  - Tracks per-request `hit -> tip` transitions directly at cache-hit (`add_local_computed_blocks`) and cache-write (`cache_blocks`, `_cache_partial_tail_block`, `cache_blocks_on_free`) sites in O(1), with no `block_hashes` scanning or boundary recomputation.
  - Preserves `t-1` rollback fallbacks, shared system-prompt junctions (`shared_prefix_boundary`), multi-branch fork points, and still-referenced blocks (`ref_cnt > 0`) in normal LRU.
- Always-on by default for prefix-cached hybrid Mamba models with zero new CLI flags or tuning knobs; updates rendered documentation in `docs/design/hybrid_kv_cache_manager.md` and `docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md`.
- Replaying real `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` AgentX traces through `KVCacheManager` using exact GB200 KV cache geometries verified via vLLM startup (`prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, `max_model_len=262144`):
  - **15/15 wins (0 regressions)** vs baseline LRU across `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` (4× GB200), `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B` (BF16 & NVFP4, 1× GB200), and `NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4` (BF16-KV & FP8-KV, 2× GB200): **-2.70% to -13.73%** total recompute tokens (**-13.73%** on `Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-BF16`, **-12.86%** on `Nemotron-3-Super-120B-NVFP4`, **-13.71%** on `Qwen3.8` FP8-KV).
  - By contrast, immediate `t-1` demotion (`prepend_k0` / `deprio_k0` as in #63808/#64975) **regresses on 9/15 configurations** (up to **+12.44%** on `Qwen3.8`, **+23.06%** on `Nemotron-3-Super-120B` `hbs=64`, and **+41.74%** on `Nemotron-3-Nano-30B` `hbs=64`) due to coding-agent tail rollbacks.

## Validation

Verified on NVIDIA GB200 nodes (merged with `main` `e59fb18b4c`):

### Unit & E2E Tests

```bash
# Targeted Mamba superseded-state tests (HEAD ddc59ee1fb)
source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -x -q --tb=short tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py -k "mamba_deprioritize"
# 6 passed, 244 deselected in 3.60s

# Full prefix caching suite (commit 48996ef0e7, prior to moving logic into MambaManager)
source .venv/bin/activate && python -m pytest -q --tb=short tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py
# 249 passed in 82.66s (0:01:22)

# FreeKVCacheBlockQueue._cached_head tests (commit c95fbcea69)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py -k "free_kv_cache_block_queue"
# 14 passed, 113 deselected in 4.64s

# Core KV cache regression suites (initial commit 377196ce01)
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --tb=short tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/ --ignore=tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py
# 352 passed in 175.98s (0:02:55)

# E2E hybrid prefix cache hit-rate test on GB200 GPU (Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B, base + MTP, commit 377196ce01)
source .venv/bin/activate && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 python -m pytest -q --tb=short tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py
# 2 passed, 18 warnings in 246.24s (0:04:06)

# Linters / docs / type checks (HEAD ddc59ee1fb)
source .venv/bin/activate && pre-commit run
# ruff check, ruff format, typos, check-test-tethering, mypy, check-docstring-style, signoff-commit: all Passed
```

*Note: Full end-to-end `vllm bench serve` throughput benchmarks on real weights are not yet included; above numbers measure exact `KVCacheManager` hit-rate / recompute-token impact on real AgentX traces with verified GB200 KV geometries.*

## Details

### Motivation & Root Cause

Full-attention KV blocks are **cumulative** (every earlier block `0..t` remains needed by turn `t+1`), whereas Mamba/GDN/PLE recurrent states are **Markovian** (turn `t+1` needs only one checkpoint at the resume boundary). Under plain recency-only LRU with `prefix_cache_retention_interval=0`, superseded checkpoints from turns `1..t-2` accumulate across every Mamba KV cache group (e.g., 4 blocks/turn on `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` and `Nemotron-3-Nano-30B`; 5 blocks/turn on `Nemotron-3-Super-120B`), reaching 35%–61% of the shared GPU block pool and evicting active sessions' full-attention KV blocks.

However, immediately demoting `t-1` (`k=0`, as in #63808 and #64975) causes cliff regressions on real coding-agent traces—especially with fine-grained prefix hashing (`hbs=64`): when turn `t+1` diverges by a few hundred tokens near the prompt tail (e.g., `<system-reminder>` edits, tool retries, or subagent edits), losing `t-1` leaves no fallback checkpoint behind `t` and collapses the prefix hit from ~45K+ tokens to `0` (+10.6% to +41.7% recompute regression on Nemotron-3 `hbs=64`).

### Design

All tracking and deprioritization live inside `MambaManager` (`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`), keeping `KVCacheManager` and `BlockPool` completely untouched (with a small generic `manager.reset_prefix_cache()` dispatch in `KVCacheCoordinator.reset_prefix_cache()`):

- **`_req_hit: dict[str, BlockHash]`** & **`_req_tip: dict[str, tuple[int, BlockHash]]`**: record the resumed Mamba state in `add_local_computed_blocks()` and the deepest newly cached state (`(num_tokens, BlockHash)`) via `_record_tip()` whenever `cache_blocks()` / `_cache_partial_tail_block()` / `cache_blocks_on_free()` caches a block; both are popped on release (`cache_blocks_on_free()` / `pop_blocks_for_free()`).
- **`_tips: dict[BlockHash, BlockHash | None]`**: maps each tracked tip in this Mamba group to:
  - `None`: leaf tip with no tracked predecessor;
  - `BlockHash`: leaf tip whose `t-1` rollback fallback is that hash;
  - `_FALLBACK_TIP` (`BlockHash(b"")`): `t-1` fallback (already extended once).
- **Deprioritization on free** (`cache_blocks_on_free()` -> `_deprioritize_superseded_state()`): after caching any decode-crossed resume block, read `hit_hash` and `tip_hash` directly in O(1):
  - **One-turn fallback (`k=1`)**: advancing `hit_hash -> tip_hash` promotes `hit_hash` to `_FALLBACK_TIP`, links `tips[tip_hash] = hit_hash`, and deprioritizes only `prev = tips[hit_hash]` (`t-2`) via `block_pool.deprioritize_blocks()`. Because `prev` is two turns behind the finishing request, its `ref_cnt` is already `0` unless another reader holds it—in which case `deprioritize_blocks()` leaves it untouched.
  - **System-prompt / shared-prefix protection**:
    1. Shared-prefix junctions (`request.shared_prefix_boundary`, populated unconditionally by the scheduler when full-attention hits deeper than Mamba) are popped from `_tips` and never tracked.
    2. Multi-branch fork points (a cached state extended by two different continuations, detected when `tips[hit_hash] == _FALLBACK_TIP`) are popped from `_tips` so shared system-prompt checkpoints remain in normal LRU.
  - **Preempted / aborted requests**: pop `_req_hit` and return without deprioritizing earlier states.
- **Documentation**: updated `docs/design/hybrid_kv_cache_manager.md` and `docs/features/automatic_prefix_caching.md`.

### AI Assistance

AI assistance (Antigravity) was used to analyze trace workloads, implement the changes and tests, and draft this PR description; all changed lines and test/replay results were reviewed and verified.

commits.pr_title: [Security] Reserve HF tokenizer options in chat requests
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Validate request-provided chat template options before the Hugging Face renderer merges them with server defaults. The validation runs in shared chat preprocessing and in chat-shaped pooling preprocessing.

## Claims

- Reserve tokenizer controls for the server and return HTTP 400 for request overrides.
- Continue accepting ordinary template variables. Cover the validation through Chat Completions, tokenization, and pooling entry points.

## Validation

Reviewed patch at `bba1153c0f93a3ca2f4744ea2bae3ccd27c591eb`, based on `9e8b3fb83ed4f3da1ed5376083027b14994939fc`.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/renderers/test_hf.py -k request_tokenizer_options
```

`4 passed, 79 deselected, 1 warning in 1.19s`

On a local CPU-only render server with the OPT-125m tokenizer, chat tokenization and chat rendering returned HTTP 200 for a benign reserved option on the base and HTTP 400 with the patch. Both builds returned HTTP 200 for an ordinary template variable. The local pooling preprocessor accepted the ordinary variable and rejected the reserved option with the expected field name. Commit hooks passed, including the Buildkite test selection check.

The full model-backed entrypoint tests are selected by Buildkite and are pending.

## Details

The renderer validates the request dictionary before its keys can be interpreted as tokenizer configuration. It uses the renderer's reserved keys so other tokenizer backends retain their existing request handling. The new tests check the validation response with bounded inputs.

A search of open and merged renderer and tokenization PRs found no equivalent request validation. #67348 limits ordinary tokenization and #68664 concerns pooling operator defaults.

This PR was developed with AI assistance.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][KV Offload] Offload the prompt tail of every attention group
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

With more than one attention KV cache group whose prompt ends inside a block, `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` never gets a fine-grained hit from the CPU tier: the finish-time flush only stores the prompt-tail block of the first full-attention group. This PR stores the tail of every group that keys one.

Related: #68837 (independent fix for the same symptom in coarse hit mode, see "Relation to other PRs"), #67547, #66234.

## Claims

- A hybrid model (prefix-cached Mamba + attention) with a second attention group of a different block size now gets fine-grained CPU hits. The case that motivated this is DCP: the target attention group is sharded (`block_size * dcp_world_size`), a full-attention draft group is replicated (`block_size`), so a prompt usually ends inside a block of both.
- On 8x MI355X with Kimi-K3.1-Pro, a full-attention DSpark draft and DCP 8, the host hit after dropping the GPU prefix cache goes from 0 to the prompt's last hash boundary: 89.1% of an 8k request with a 7,360-token prefix, 90.0% of a 100k request with a 90,112-token prefix.
- No change for layouts with a single attention group, for lazy offload, or when fine-grained hits are off.

## Validation

**Unit test, fails on main and passes here** (real `Scheduler` + `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, CPU only; a prefix-cached Mamba group, a DCP-sharded target group and a replicated full-attention draft group; prime a 150-token prompt, reset the GPU prefix cache only, send the prompt plus a suffix):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py -k dcp_hybrid -v
```

main `2b55f82b0`:

```
E       assert 0 == 148
FAILED tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py::test_dcp_hybrid_offloads_prompt_tail_of_every_attention_group
====================== 1 failed, 90 deselected in 16.94s =======================
```

this PR:

```
====================== 1 passed, 90 deselected in 16.51s =======================
```

**Affected suites** (one GPU visible so the device type resolves):

```bash
python -m pytest tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/simple_kv_offload/test_kv_events.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_simple_cpu_offload_connector.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache \
  tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_mamba_align_chunk_split.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_hybrid.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_umbp_core.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/moriio/test_moriio_hma_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py
```

On this head (base `2b55f82b0`): 2069 passed, 2 errors. The 2 errors are the setup of `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py`, which starts a server with real weights that this environment does not have; it errors the same way on main.

`pre-commit run --from-ref upstream/main --to-ref HEAD` passes (mypy run separately under Python 3.12: no issues).

**Scheduler-level reproduction at the real geometry.** The real `Scheduler`, `KVCacheManager` and the scheduler side of SimpleCPU, driven on CPU with the group layout the engine logs for Kimi-K3.1-Pro under DCP 8 (`kv cache group sizes (1152, 1152, 1152, 9216, 1152)`: three Mamba groups, the sharded target group, the replicated draft group), `--prefix-match-unit 64`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`. 16 prefixes are primed, the GPU prefix cache is reset (`reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=False)`), then each prefix is sent with a new suffix. Host-hit share of the prompt tokens, base `8ca766326652` with and without this change:

| draft group | request | base | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| full attention | 8,192 tokens, 7,360-token prefix | 0% (16 x 0) | 89.1% (16 x 7,296) |
| full attention | 100,000 tokens, 90,112-token prefix | 0% (16 x 0) | 90.0% (16 x 90,048) |
| sliding window | either | unchanged (coarse hit mode, see #68837 / #67547) | unchanged |

**End to end, one 8x MI355X node, TP 8 + DCP 8, Kimi-K3.1-Pro with a DSpark draft, fp8 KV, eager SimpleCPU offload** (`vllm/vllm-openai-rocm` nightly at `8ca766326652`; the patched servers overlay this change as it applies to that commit, i.e. before #66234 reworked the boundary computation; the per-group loop is the same). All servers ran back to back in one session. Same procedure as the reproduction, through `/v1/completions` with token-id prompts and `/reset_prefix_cache?reset_external=false`; hits read from `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `vllm:prompt_tokens_cached_by_source_total`. Each cell is the host-hit share of the prompt tokens of 16 requests at concurrency 16.

| code | draft | 8k request (7,360 prefix) | 100k request (90,112 prefix) |
|---|---|---|---|
| base | full attention | 0% (16 x 0) | 0% (16 x 0) |
| **this PR** | full attention | **89.1%** (16 x 7,296) | **90.0%** (16 x 90,048) |
| base | sliding window | 0% (16 x 0) | 10.4% (2 x 82,944, 14 x 0) |
| this PR | sliding window | 0% (16 x 0) | 10.4% (2 x 82,944, 14 x 0) |
| this PR + #67547 | sliding window | 89.1% (16 x 7,296) | 90.0% (16 x 90,048) |
| this PR + #68837 + #67547 | sliding window | 89.1% (16 x 7,296) | 90.0% (16 x 90,048) |

With this PR and the full-attention draft, the TTFT of a host hit at concurrency 1 is 0.18 s (8k) and 1.42 s (100k); a cold request on the same node takes 1.14 s and 13.37 s (measured on the base server with the sliding-window draft). Rows 3 and 4 are the coarse-mode case this PR does not touch.

<details>
<summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1 \
  VLLM_FASTSAFETENSORS_QUEUE_SIZE=-1 VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm \
  VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FLYDSL_SPARSE_MLA=1 AITER_FLYDSL_SPARSE_MLA=1 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 \
  VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=0 \
  VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=NONE AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1 \
  THP_MEM_ALLOC_ENABLE=0 VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=1 VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro --trust-remote-code --language-model-only \
  --block-size 1152 --load-format fastsafetensors --max-model-len 1048576 --enable-prefix-caching \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
  --prefix-match-unit 64 --moe-backend auto --seed 7 --max-num-seqs 24 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --prefill-schedule-interval 32 --enable-prompt-tokens-details \
  --additional-config '{"kda_prefill_backend":"fused"}' \
  --compilation-config '{"mode":3,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_AND_PIECEWISE","custom_ops":["+fused_rms_norm_gated"]}' \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"<draft>","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":48000000000,"lazy_offload":false}}'
```

`<draft>` is `LithosAI/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark` (full attention) or `Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark` (sliding window); `cudagraph_capture_sizes` omitted here. Patched servers run the same image with only the changed Python files overlaid.
</details>

**Output check, this PR alone with the full-attention draft** (same server as row 2; greedy, real block rejection, `/v1/chat/completions`, thinking off).

- Five natural-text prompts (3 of about 8k tokens, 2 of about 100k) answered cold, cold again, from a device hit, from a host hit of the same prompt, and from a host hit of a 90% prefix, with `logprobs`. All 25 runs give the same final answer per prompt. Greedy text is not bit-stable even cold against cold (0 of 5 identical here), so each run is compared with the first cold run token by token: over the leading tokens that agree, the largest logprob difference is 0.19 for the cold repeat, 0.49 for the device hit, 0.28 for the host hit and 0.23 for the host hit of a prefix. Host hits deviate no more than device hits do.
- Few-shot GSM8K, 240 questions, each with its own 8 solved examples so every prompt is unique and about 1,430 tokens: a cold pass, then a GPU-only cache reset and the same prompts again. Cold pass 99.17%; second pass 98.75% with all 240 requests served from host hits (335,040 of 343,265 prompt tokens), same prediction on 239 of 240 questions. On a server without the connector (sliding-window draft, so a different absolute level) two cold passes give 97.92% and 97.50% and agree on 234 of 240, which is the pass-to-pass spread to compare against.
- Zero-shot GSM8K (1,319 questions) on the base server without the connector: 97.35%.

## Details

**Root cause.** In fine-grained mode a hybrid lookup must hit on every prefix-cacheable group at the same hash boundary. Full blocks reach the CPU through the positional eager scan and prefix-cached Mamba states through the boundary-state hand-off, but a prompt tail that ends inside an attention block is only keyed as a partial entry on that block and is copied by `_queue_finished_eager_store` when the request finishes. That code resolved one group, `fa_gidx`, the first `FullAttentionManager` group. With a replicated draft group next to the DCP-sharded target group there are two such groups; the second one's tail was never stored, its CPU lookup stopped at its last full block, the Mamba groups had no state there, and the combined hit was 0.

**Change.** `_find_fa_partial_tail_source` becomes `_find_partial_tail_source(request, block_ids, group_idx)` and the flush calls it for every prefix-cacheable group. Nothing else in the selection changes: a block is taken only if the prompt's last hash boundary is actually registered on it, null blocks (e.g. sliding-window pages that left the window) and in-flight blocks are skipped, an existing CPU entry is skipped, and the CPU free-block budget is checked per appended block. prefix-cached Mamba groups return early (their block tables are not positional and their tail already arrives through the hand-off). The cost is at most one more block copy per extra group when a request finishes.

`fa_gidx` / `fa_block_size` are left in place (construction-time assert, used by existing tests).

**Relation to other PRs.**

- #68837 fixes a second, independent cause of the same symptom (a hybrid model with several KV cache groups getting no CPU hits). It touches `vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py` and applies in coarse hit mode; this PR touches `vllm/v1/simple_kv_offload/manager.py` and applies in fine-grained mode. Neither depends on the other and they can merge in either order. Both add the same test helper (`_make_dcp_hybrid_engine`, `_run_engine_request`, and a `scheduler_block_size` argument for `create_scheduler`) with identical text; whichever lands second gets rebased.
- #67547 (fine-grained hits for sliding-window groups) makes a sliding-window draft group key a prompt tail too. With SimpleCPU and several attention groups that PR needs this one to get host hits: in the scheduler-level reproduction #67547 alone gives 0% host hits for both draft types, #67547 plus this PR gives 89.1% / 90.0%. The registered-key check here picks such groups up without further changes. The two PRs conflict textually on one docstring line of the renamed function.
- #66234 (merged) changed the same function; this PR is rebased on it and keeps its boundary computation (`get_reusable_prefix_length`).

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs for `SimpleCPUOffload`, `simple_kv_offload`, "partial tail", "prompt tail" and grepped the diffs of the candidates (#49962, #57325, #60742, #61375, #66234, #67547, #67952, #68511): none stores the tail of more than one group. #68670 (draft) adds draft-group pages to the UMBP connector's hand-offs and does not touch SimpleCPU.

**CI coverage.** The new test runs in the existing `tests/v1/simple_kv_offload` step. The end-to-end configuration needs a multi-GPU DCP deployment of a hybrid model with a draft model, which CI does not have; it was validated outside CI as described above.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the code, tests and this description.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Classify multimodal preprocessing errors by fault
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`vllm_chat::Error::Multimodal(String)` flattens llm-multimodal's tracker, transform and model spec errors into a string, so `Error::kind()` (vllm-project/vllm#68933) cannot tell a request fault from a server fault: the chat routes answer all of them 500, while gRPC render answers all of them `INVALID_ARGUMENT` and HTTP render answers them 400 through #68933's interim arm. This PR keeps those errors typed and classifies each inner category in `Error::kind()`, so chat and render (HTTP and gRPC) give one answer: the request's fault is 400, a media host timeout or an internal preprocessing failure is 500. It is a sibling of vllm-project/vllm#70091 (renderer refusals), not stacked on it.

## Claims

| Error | Before (chat / gRPC render / HTTP render) | After (all three) |
|---|---|---|
| `MediaConnectorError` with `MediaFault::Client` | 400 / 400 / 400 | 400 |
| `MediaConnectorError` transient or internal (host timeout, decoder I/O) | 500 / 400 / 500 | 500 |
| `MultiModalError::UnsupportedContent` | 500 / 400 / 400 | 400 |
| `MultiModalError::Join`, `Validation` (tracker task and invariant) | 500 / 400 / 400 | 500 |
| `TransformError::DecodedTooLarge` | 500 / 400 / 400 | 400 |
| `TransformError::{InvalidShape, EmptyBatch, InconsistentShapes, ShapeError}` | 500 / 400 / 400 | 500 |
| `ModelRegistryError::{ModalityLimitExceeded, UnsupportedModality}` | 500 / 400 / 400 | 400 |
| other `ModelRegistryError` (model files and config) | 500 / 400 / 400 | 500 |
| `Error::Multimodal(String)` (this crate's own preparation failures) | 500 / 400 / 400 | 500 |

- gRPC render drops its `Multimodal(_) | Media(_)` → `INVALID_ARGUMENT` clause and reads `kind()`; HTTP render drops the `Multimodal` arm of the interim mapping.

## Validation

On head `8d3e5ed971` (base `main` `5b5b371e32`), with the commands of `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh`:

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [  12.895s] 2945 tests run: 2945 passed, 13 skipped`

Red-green:
- `vllm-chat` `error::tests::multimodal_error_is_request_validation_error_only_when_the_request_is_at_fault` (extends the existing media table): with #68933's classification, the four request faults (unsupported content part, decoded-size cap, modality limit, unsupported modality) come out as server errors (500); with this PR, as request errors.
- `vllm-server` `grpc::render::tests::chat_errors_map_to_status_like_the_chat_routes`: with the old OR clause a media host timeout is `INVALID_ARGUMENT`; with this PR, `INTERNAL`.

There is no route-level test: the fake chat backend cannot produce a typed llm-multimodal request fault through a real request without a processor spec that refuses it; the transports only map `ErrorKind`, which both tests pin at their boundary.

## Details

**Ownership and layering.** The classification lives in `vllm_chat::Error::kind()`, the single owner #68933 established for request-vs-server classification, so every entry point reads one answer and the transports only map `ErrorKind` to a status. `Media` now wraps the whole `MultiModalError` (tracker errors, of which a media fetch is one) next to `MultimodalTransform` and `MultimodalSpec`; `Error::Multimodal(String)` stays for this crate's own preparation failures (placeholder tokenization, processor config files, renderer and tracker invariants), all server-side.

**Where Rust differs from Python.**
- Python wraps every exception an HF processor raises in `ValueError` (`vllm/multimodal/processing/context.py`, "Failed to apply …"), so a checkpoint's unusable processor config is also a 400 there. That is incidental to how the call is wrapped, not a request contract; Rust keeps tensor shape errors and the model's own config server-side.
- `TransformError::ShapeError` also carries geometry refusals of the request's media (Step3-VL refusing a 100000x32 image), which Python answers 400. These stay 500 with a TODO in `transform_error_kind` until their producers report them apart, which needs a new llm-multimodal variant. On render this is a 400 → 500 change; the chat routes already answer it 500 on `main`.
- A trusted request `chat_template` that drops the image placeholder fails the placeholder expansion after rendering, where Rust cannot tell a request template from the checkpoint's; it stays 500 (it needs `--trust-request-chat-template`, and the chat routes answer it 500 on `main`), and on render it changes from 400 to 500. Typing that mismatch with its provenance is a follow-up.
- Client-fault media errors stay 400 where Python answers 422 for some of them (vllm-project/vllm#47165), matching the OpenAI API.
- Messages lose the `multimodal preprocessing error:` prefix for the newly typed errors (they are transparent now); no test pins that prefix.

**Related PRs.** vllm-project/vllm#70091 types renderer refusals and also edits `Error::kind()` and the interim arms of `render_chat`; the two are independent, and whichever lands second takes a mechanical rebase of `rust/src/server/src/routes/render.rs`. HTTP `/inference/v1/generate` maps every `prepare_media` error to 400, unlike gRPC inference, which reads `kind()`; that is pre-existing and left for the same provenance follow-up.

**Not a duplicate.** vllm-project/vllm#68309 changes the HTTP status of client-fault media errors to 422; this PR keeps them at 400 and classifies the tracker, transform and model spec errors, which no open PR does.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex (changes needed: the two render 400 → 500 cases above, kept and documented since telling them apart needs typed producers; two non-blocking points documented). I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Preserve the first reasoning boundary in speculative drafts
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fixes #68277.

A speculative draft that closes and then reopens thinking can remove the JSON constraint from an accepted shorter prefix. Preserve the first reasoning-end boundary so the invalid opener is masked before sampling.

Use Kimi's first-close lookup, single-token checks for the shared fallback, and token-view slices that avoid copying the full history. This consolidates QwertyJack's singleton-delta optimization into the existing fix.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py \
  tests/v1/test_request.py tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py \
  -k 'not mask and (kimi or token_ids_view or single_token_checks or clear_backend_without_grammar)' -q
```

CPU (macOS ARM64, Python 3.12): `140 passed, 84 deselected, 9 warnings in 18.40s`. The close/reopen regression fails all 8 cases before the fix (`26 != 13`, etc.) and passes all 8 after it. The four mask cases require accelerator CI.

The full Linux pre-commit job, including mypy 1.20.2, [passed on this commit](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/45739115944/job/139639503805).

Downstream Ascend adaptation: 100/100 HTTP replays and 10/10 multi-turn requests passed through direct decode; these runs did not exercise the full PD path. [Validation report](https://github.com/linnea-lin-00638949/vllm/blob/bd7becdc9d/review_artifacts/pr68112/generation-regression.md).

## Performance

CPU boundary lookup, 32K-token history; median microseconds per call:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Thinking, 7 draft tokens | 362.78 | 1.06 |
| Close → reopen | 361.34 | 1.82 |
| Split close → reopen, 29 draft tokens | 361.33 | 64.30 |

The unfixed code returns the wrong boundary in the last two cases. [Benchmark details](https://github.com/linnea-lin-00638949/vllm/blob/bd7becdc9d/review_artifacts/pr68112/integration-performance.md); these measure the helper, not serving throughput.

AI assistance was used for implementation and testing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Swizzle mxfp8 activation scales after DP/EP dispatch for FlashInfer CUTLASS
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `--data-parallel-size > 1`, mxfp8 activation scales reach the FlashInfer CUTLASS MXFP4/MXFP8 MoE kernel in row-major layout instead of the swizzled 128x4 layout it expects. This swizzles them after the dispatch, as nvfp4 scales already are.

This is #49335 by @Wollac rebased onto current main, with his design and test kept (credited as co-author), plus a compute-capability skip so the test does not fail on the L4 CI runner. Fixes #42118. Fixes #67575. cc @mgoin (filed #42118)

## Claims

- Fixes the startup illegal memory access with `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS_MXFP4_MXFP8` under data parallel + expert parallel. We reproduced the crash on SM120 (2x RTX 5090), and this PR resolves it. The wrong or NaN output reported in #42118 and #67575 comes from the same out-of-bounds read of the scales; we did not observe it in our runs.
- One helper, `restore_dispatched_scale_layout`, replaces the nvfp4-only inline swizzle in the naive DP/EP and both FlashInfer NVLink prepare/finalize paths.
- nvfp4 is unchanged: the naive-path nvfp4 scales are byte-identical before and after (16 cases). Kernels that take unswizzled scales (e.g. `FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_MXFP8`) still get their scales as is.

## Validation

Environment: 2x NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (SM120), torch 2.14.0+cu130, flashinfer 0.7.4, vLLM nightly `0.34.0rc1.dev897+g9c1d45c21` with this change applied as a patch. The GPU runs used the change before its last commit edit, which only adds the test's SM100 skip. None of the 77 commits between `9c1d45c21` and this PR's base `ab91867b5` touch the changed files, `fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py` or the MoE runner.

**Reported vs. reproduced here** (2x RTX 5090, SM120):

| Reported | Where | Here |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong output, gpt-oss-20b, DP=2 + EP | #42118 | Not observed; our runs crashed at startup instead (same out-of-bounds read) |
| Illegal memory access at startup, DP=2 + EP | #67575 (16x RTX 6000D, SM120) | Reproduced on main |
| Garbage output, or an illegal access with the caching allocator off | #67575 comment (2x RTX PRO 6000, SM120) | Crash reproduced; garbage not observed |
| The one-line gate fix resolves it | #67575 | Confirmed with this PR: server starts, 8 of 8 prompts correct |

**End to end, same command on main and on this PR** (the model and flags from #42118, plus the explicit backend):

```bash
vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass \
  --quantization-config '{"moe":{"activation":"mxfp8"}}' \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 2 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --max-model-len 4096 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.6 --enforce-eager
```

- main: the server dies during startup with an illegal memory access. With `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` the failure surfaces inside `flashinfer.fused_moe.core.cutlass_fused_moe` (called from `fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py`) as a CUTLASS grouped-GEMM initialization assertion.
- this PR: the server starts and answers 8 of 8 fixed greedy prompts correctly. On one GPU with data parallel 1 (the path without the bug), all 8 are also correct; 5 of 8 match token for token over 12 tokens, and 3 diverge only after the correct answer.

<details>
<summary>main: raw error</summary>

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'Check failed: (status == cudaSuccess) is false: BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache failed with error an illegal memory access was encountered', please check the stack

# rerun with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1:
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/modular_kernel.py", line 1509, in _fused_experts
  File ".../vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/experts/flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py", line 372, in apply
  File ".../flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py", line 1925, in cutlass_fused_moe
  File ".../flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py", line 1361, in cutlass_fused_moe
Assertion failed: Failed to initialize cutlass TMA WS grouped gemm. Error: Error Internal (.../cutlass_instantiations/120/gemm_grouped/120/cutlass_kernel_file_gemm_grouped_sm120_M128_BS_...
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>this PR: raw output (temperature 0, max_tokens 12)</summary>

```
'17*23='                   -> '391, 391-1=390, 390/'
'2+2='                     -> '4, 2+3=5, 2+'
'The capital of France is' -> ' Paris."\n\nSure! Here\'s a simple example of a Python'
'10-3='                    -> '7, 7%2=1, so no.\n\n'
'Q: 5+8? A:'               -> ' 13. So 5+8=13. So'
'The opposite of hot is'   -> ' cold.\n\nThe opposite of hot is cold.\n\nThe'
'12*12='                   -> '144, 12*12=144, 12*'
'100/4='                   -> '25. So 25*4=100. So '
```
</details>

**New test** (`tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp8_dp_scale_swizzle.py`, from #49335):

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_mxfp8_dp_scale_swizzle.py
```

- SM120, this PR: `13 passed, 49 warnings in 14.71s` (before the SM100 skip was added; the skip does not apply on SM120)
- main: the file fails at import (the helper it tests does not exist on main). A main-compatible variant of the same byte-for-byte check, calling `_unwrap_scale_and_prepare_for_moe` directly, fails on all 21 mxfp8 shapes on main (e.g. 1 token at hidden 2048: the scales come back as `[1, 64]` where the kernel expects the 8192-byte swizzled buffer) and passes on all 22 with this PR, including hidden size 2880 (gpt-oss; 90 scale columns, not a multiple of 4).
- L4 (SM89, the CI runner for `kernels/moe`): `1 skipped`. FlashInfer's mxfp8 quantization raises `ValueError: Invalid backend: 89` below SM100, so without the skip the file fails 13 of 13 there (checked).

CI coverage: the CI GPUs for this test folder cannot run mxfp8, so CI only checks that the file skips cleanly; the SM120 results above are the validation. The NVLink one-sided and two-sided paths get the same one-line change but could not be run on PCIe hardware.

Lint: `pre-commit run --files` on the 5 changed files: all 17 applicable hooks pass (ruff check, ruff format, typos, mypy, SPDX headers, the new-test CI wiring check and others), 0 fail.

## Details

Root cause: the DP/EP prepare paths quantize with `is_scale_swizzled=False` before the all-to-all, because the swizzled layout is padded and does not line up row for row with the hidden states. After the all-to-all they swizzle again, but only `if quant_dtype == "nvfp4"`, so mxfp8 scales stay row-major, and the CUTLASS kernel reads past them.

Change: `restore_dispatched_scale_layout(a1q_scale, quant_dtype, is_scale_swizzled)` in `fused_moe/utils.py` returns the scales unchanged unless the kernel wants swizzled scales and the dtype is `nvfp4` or `mxfp8`; then it views 1-byte scales as `uint8` and calls the existing `block_scale_interleave` wrapper. By code reading it adds no host synchronization (no `.item()`, `.cpu()` or data-dependent branching on GPU values). The three prepare paths call it in place of their inline code.

No other open PR fixes #42118 or #67575; #42133 was closed in May.

AI assistance: the rebase, the conflict resolution, the validation runs and this description were prepared with an AI assistant. The non-test code is byte-identical to #49335's change, re-targeted to main's new one-sided dispatch path.

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Accept only OpenAI's input_audio format names
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Make `input_audio.format` a required `wav`/`mp3` value in the Rust frontend's chat, `/tokenize` and Responses request types, as the OpenAI API and Python's request types define it. Today Rust accepts `WAV`, `MP3` and a missing format, and fails on an unknown name only later, during media preparation.

## Claims

- On `/v1/chat/completions`, `/tokenize` and `/v1/responses`, an `input_audio` part with `"format": "WAV"`, `"MP3"`, `null`, a missing `format`, or `"flac"` is a 400; `wav` and `mp3` work as before.
- `/tokenize` treats a body whose `messages` is a list as a chat request, so a malformed chat part beside a `prompt` is a 400 instead of silently tokenizing `prompt`.
- gRPC Render keeps its optional `format` field (absent: the connector detects the container), matched case-insensitively; an unknown name is now `INVALID_ARGUMENT` at lowering for every renderer.

## Validation

On head `aa24af439c` (base `main` `5b5b371e32`):

```
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check
cargo sort --workspace --check rust
cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans
cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast
```

`Summary [  10.595s] 2950 tests run: 2950 passed, 13 skipped`

- `chat_http_input_audio_format_accepts_only_openai_names`: `wav`/`mp3` accepted in a chat request; missing, `null`, `WAV`, `MP3`, `flac` rejected, with the field's own error at the `InputAudio` type. `input_audio_requires_an_openai_format_name` does the same for the Responses type.
- `tokenize_selects_chat_by_a_messages_list`: `WAV` in a `messages` list beside `prompt` is a 400; `messages: null` or `17` beside `prompt` still tokenizes `prompt`.
- `responses_input_audio_requires_format`: a Responses `input_audio` part without `format` is a 400.
- `input_audio_format_is_optional_but_must_name_wav_or_mp3` (gRPC lowering): absent, `wav` and `MP3` accepted; `flac` and empty rejected.
- Red-green: with the production change reverted, the chat and Responses type tests fail (`format None must be rejected`). With the strict part type but the old untagged `/tokenize` request enum, `/tokenize` returned 200 with the six tokens of `hello`.
- Target check against the OpenAI API (chat completions): `WAV` and `MP3` → 400 `Invalid value: 'WAV'. Supported values are: 'wav' and 'mp3'.`; missing → 400 `missing_required_parameter`; `null` → 400 `invalid_type`; `flac` → 400 `invalid_value`. Python's `ChatCompletionRequest` on `main` accepts `wav`/`mp3` and raises a validation error (400) for the other five.

## Details

**Root cause.** OpenAI defines `input_audio.format` as required with exactly `wav` and `mp3`, and Python's chat request types reuse the SDK's `InputAudio` TypedDict (`format: Required[Literal["wav", "mp3"]]`). The Rust frontend kept `format` as an optional string and matched it case-insensitively in `vllm-chat` (`input_audio_data_url`), so chat and `/tokenize` accepted `WAV`/`MP3` and a missing format (sent to the media connector as `application/octet-stream`). Only an unknown name failed, and only during media preparation. The Responses converter required `format` but also accepted uppercase names.

**Change.**
- `vllm_chat::multimodal::InputAudioFormat { Wav, Mp3 }`: serde takes OpenAI's lowercase names, `FromStr` ignores case. `ChatContentPart::InputAudio.format` is `Option<InputAudioFormat>`; `None` means the container is not named, which only gRPC Render produces. `input_audio_data_url` maps the enum to a MIME type and can no longer fail, so `Error::UnsupportedInputAudioFormat` is removed.
- The HTTP `InputAudio` type (shared by chat, `/tokenize` and Responses) has a required `format: InputAudioFormat`, so the check happens where the wire is parsed; the Responses converter's own `format` check is gone.
- `/tokenize` selects its variant by whether `messages` is a list instead of `#[serde(untagged)]`. With the stricter part type, the untagged enum would fall back to the completion variant for a body carrying both a malformed `messages` list and `prompt`, and answer 200 with the tokens of `prompt`; Python treats such a body as a chat request.
- gRPC Render parses its optional, case-insensitive name into the same enum, so `flac` fails at lowering whichever renderer serves the request (before, a text-only renderer that skips media accepted it). The proto comment names the two values.

**Differences from Python.** A malformed `input_audio.format` on chat and Responses answers serde's generic `data did not match any variant of untagged enum ...` message, because message content stays `#[serde(untagged)]`; surfacing the failing part's own error is a separate change. Python's Responses request model does not accept `input_audio` parts at all (vllm-project/vllm#64851 proposes adding them), so Rust's Responses support is wider; it uses the same strict names as chat.

**Not a duplicate.** No open PR makes the Rust `input_audio.format` strict. vllm-project/vllm#69671 (images and audio in Responses `function_call_output`) builds `input_audio` parts with a string `format`; whichever lands second takes a mechanical type adaptation.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code and reviewed by Codex over three rounds, each "changes needed": the `/tokenize` fallback to `prompt`, gRPC Render's case-insensitive names and `/tokenize` selecting chat only for a `messages` list were fixed; rejecting an unknown gRPC name for renderers that skip media, and the round 3 findings, were declined. A JSON-type dispatch of message content that surfaced the part's own error was later split out of this PR. I reviewed every changed line.

commits.pr_title: [Model][Perf] HY4: Use the fused iHC boundary op on all paths and fuse HY4 Flash q/kv-a projections
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #68770. All iHC steps on NVIDIA now run through the CUDA `hy_v4_ihc_boundary` op, and the HY4 Flash `q_a_proj` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` GEMMs are fused into one.

## Claims

- HY4 TP / TEP (iHC sequence parallel with `defer_reduction`) now builds the fused boundaries. Before this PR it fell back to Triton / HPC pre + post + RMSNorm at every boundary.
- A lone iHC post step, and the last post together with the head and the final norm, reuse the same boundary op. No CUDA change was needed.
- HY4 Flash fuses `q_a_proj` and `kv_a_proj_with_mqa` into one `MergedColumnParallelLinear` GEMM.
- Accuracy is unchanged for HY4 Flash under TP4, TEP4 and DEP4.

## Validation

Tests run on commit `84a45123c9`:

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_hy_v4_ihc_boundary.py
118 passed in 39.11s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/hy_v4/test_sequence_parallel.py
2 passed, 18 warnings in 422.71s (0:07:02)
```

### Accuracy 

**Hy4-flash-FP8**

| Config | gsm8k (lm-eval, chat 5-shot, flexible / strict) | AIME25 (exact_match / pass@3, 3 samples) | OCRBench |
|---|---|---|---|
| main (#68770), TP4 | 0.9659 / 0.9378 | 0.9778 / 1.0 | 830 |
| this PR, TP4 | 0.9621 / 0.9303 | 0.9556 / 1.0 | 828 |
| this PR, TEP4 | 0.9659 / 0.9378 | 0.9778 / 1.0 | 839 |
| this PR, DEP4 | 0.9666 / 0.9333 | 1.0 / 1.0 | 837 |


**HY4-FP8**
| Mode | GSM8K (boxed extraction audit) | OCRBench | AIME25 | GPQA Diamond |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TP4  | 96.36% | 86.6% | 100% | 88.89% |
| TEP4 | 97.12% | 86.3% | 100% | 91.41% |
| DEP4 | 96.74% | 86.8% | 100% | 90.91% |


### Performance(Hy4-Flash-FP8)

`vllm bench serve`, random 8192 in / 512 out. Each cell is TTFT (ms) / TPOT (ms) / output throughput (tok/s).

| Config | Concurrency | main (#68770) | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| TP4 | 1 | 226 / 6.37 / 147.5 | 226 / 6.19 / 151.1 |
| TP4 | 32 | 2108 / 17.09 / 1588 | 2098 / 16.89 / 1608 |
| TEP4 | 1 | 243 / 6.56 / 142.9 | 244 / 6.35 / 146.8 |
| TEP4 | 32 | 1787 / 18.56 / 1485 | 2322 / 17.95 / 1505 |
| DEP4 | 1 | 441 / 7.92 / 113.9 | 438 / 7.73 / 116.4 |
| DEP4 | 32 | 2931 / 12.86 / 1719 | 3448 / 13.11 / 1658 |

Median TTFT at concurrency 32 is noisy. The same main build gave 1787 ms and 2331 ms for TEP4 in two runs.

## Details

- `forward_ihc_fused` handles iHC sequence parallel. It all-gathers before attention and before the MLP. It finishes the deferred reduction with `_deferred_reduce`, which reduce-scatters under sequence parallel and all-reduces otherwise. The unfused path shares the same helper. PP is unaffected, because iHC sequence parallel requires PP=1.
- The head gate is packed as zero-padded pre rows with magnitude 1.0. `fused_post` falls back to the unfused head if the parameters were re-pointed after loading.
- The Triton / HPC iHC paths are kept as the fallback for when the op is unavailable. Removing them is left to a follow-up.
