commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Fix `model_impl="transformers"` for architectures Transformers doesn't have
commits.pr_body:
## Overview `model_impl="transformers"` fails with "Cannot find model module" for models that vLLM already serves with the Transformers backend under `model_impl="auto"`, such as InternLM3, EXAONE 3/3.5, IQuest-Coder and Sarvam (#66416, #68728). Their `architectures` (e.g. `InternLM3ForCausalLM`) is not a Transformers class, and resolution only tries `getattr(transformers, architecture)` and `auto_map`, while the backend builds the model with `AutoModel.from_config`, which only needs the config class. This PR falls back to the class `AutoModel` builds (`transformers.MODEL_MAPPING[type(hf_config)]`) unless the existing `auto_map` loop would load trusted custom code. Phi-3-vision hits the same with huggingface/transformers#51214 (open): its Hub `architectures` stays `Phi3VForCausalLM`, while Transformers names the class `Phi3VForConditionalGeneration`. No open PR or issue covers this. ## Claims - With `model_impl="transformers"` and without `trust_remote_code`, InternLM3, EXAONE 3.5, IQuest-Coder, SarvamMoE and SarvamMLA resolve to the same backend class as with `model_impl="auto"`, and Phi-3.5-vision with huggingface/transformers#51214 gives the same output without `hf_overrides` as main does with them. - Only calls that raise "Cannot find model module" on main behave differently. ## Validation `test_architecture_not_in_transformers` (Qwen3-0.6B with `architectures` overridden to `CustomQwen3ForCausalLM`, checked against the same model under its own name) fails on main and passes with this PR. On GB10, EXAONE-3.5-2.4B and InternLM3-8B, which fail on main, load and generate, and Phi-3.5-vision with huggingface/transformers#51214 gives identical output without `hf_overrides` as main with them. The config-only check of the five models and a CPU run on this PR's base are below.
Test (CPU, Apple M4; main dd0838553, this PR 982d5a7831; Transformers 5.24.1) ```bash pytest tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k test_architecture_not_in_transformers --durations=0 ``` ``` # main E pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for ModelConfig E Value error, Cannot find model module. 'CustomQwen3ForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library (only relevant if the model is meant to be in Transformers) and 'AutoModel' is not present in the model config's 'auto_map' (relevant if the model is custom). [type=value_error, input_value=ArgsKwargs((), {'model': ...nderer_num_workers': 1}), input_type=ArgsKwargs] FAILED tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_architecture_not_in_transformers ======================= 1 failed, 47 deselected in 2.50s ======================= # this PR 40.81s call tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py::test_architecture_not_in_transformers ====================== 1 passed, 47 deselected in 43.39s ======================= ```
Models served through the backend (config only, same commits) ```python mc = ModelConfig(repo, model_impl=model_impl) print(f"{repo}: {mc.architecture} -> {mc._model_info.architecture}") ``` Revisions: internlm3-8b-instruct `28c99415ad`, EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct `ccce25bd39`, IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct `265a7cba7d`, sarvam-30b `2784c524a2`, sarvam-105b `abe264bdb8`. ``` # main, model_impl="transformers" internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct: Value error, Cannot find model module. 'InternLM3ForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library … LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct: Value error, Cannot find model module. 'ExaoneForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library … IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct: Value error, Cannot find model module. 'IQuestCoderForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library … sarvamai/sarvam-30b: Value error, Cannot find model module. 'SarvamMoEForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library … sarvamai/sarvam-105b: Value error, Cannot find model module. 'SarvamMLAForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library … # main and this PR, model_impl="auto" internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct: InternLM3ForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct: ExaoneForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct: IQuestCoderForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM sarvamai/sarvam-30b: SarvamMoEForCausalLM -> TransformersMoEForCausalLM sarvamai/sarvam-105b: SarvamMLAForCausalLM -> TransformersMoEForCausalLM # this PR, model_impl="transformers" internlm/internlm3-8b-instruct: TransformersForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM LGAI-EXAONE/EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct: TransformersForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM IQuestLab/IQuest-Coder-V1-40B-Instruct: TransformersForCausalLM -> TransformersForCausalLM sarvamai/sarvam-30b: TransformersMoEForCausalLM -> TransformersMoEForCausalLM sarvamai/sarvam-105b: TransformersMoEForCausalLM -> TransformersMoEForCausalLM ```
GB10 (sm_121), torch 2.14.0+cu130: vLLM a87e3a6554 (+#66840, kernel-only) with and without this PR's change; huggingface/transformers#51214 at a845d34c25 ```python LLM(repo, revision=revision, model_impl=model_impl, dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=4096, gpu_memory_utilization=0.4, enforce_eager=True, seed=0) # Phi-3.5-vision: also limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}; main: hf_overrides as below ``` Greedy decoding. EXAONE and InternLM3 use two chat prompts with `max_tokens=32`; Phi-3.5-vision uses the two prompts from the CPU run below. On `a87e3a6554`, `model_impl="auto"` still uses vLLM's own EXAONE and InternLM3 classes (it predates #66416), so they are the reference here. | model | main, `model_impl="transformers"` | this PR, `model_impl="transformers"` | against the reference | |---|---|---|---| | Phi-3.5-vision (`12b77fb40b`) | "Cannot find model module" | `Using Transformers' Phi3VModel for Phi3VForCausalLM.` | main with `hf_overrides`: identical token ids and logprobs | | EXAONE-3.5-2.4B-Instruct (`ccce25bd39`) | "Cannot find model module" | `Using Transformers' LlamaModel for ExaoneForCausalLM.` | main `auto`: same tokens on both prompts, max \|Δ logprob\| 0.061 | | InternLM3-8B-Instruct (`28c99415ad`) | "Cannot find model module" | `Using Transformers' LlamaModel for InternLM3ForCausalLM.` | main `auto`: same 32 tokens on one prompt; on the other, after 14 equal tokens, the top token has p 0.50 (main) vs 0.47 (this PR); max \|Δ logprob\| 0.043 on shared tokens |
Phi-3.5-vision (CPU, Apple M4, bf16; main dd0838553, this PR 982d5a7831; huggingface/transformers#51214 at a845d34c25) ```python llm = LLM("microsoft/Phi-3.5-vision-instruct", revision="12b77fb40b63a2c73c68243d3f767aab688a1b2a", model_impl="transformers", dtype="bfloat16", max_model_len=2048, limit_mm_per_prompt={"image": 1}, seed=0) # main: hf_overrides={"architectures": ["Phi3VForConditionalGeneration"]}; this PR: no hf_overrides image = Image.open(requests.get("https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/pipeline-cat-chonk.jpeg", stream=True).raw).convert("RGB") prompts = [{"prompt": "<|user|>\n<|image|>\nDescribe this image in one sentence.<|end|>\n<|assistant|>\n", "multi_modal_data": {"image": [image]}}, {"prompt": "<|user|>\nWhat is the capital of France?<|end|>\n<|assistant|>\n"}] params = SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=24, stop_token_ids=[32000], logprobs=1) outs = [llm.generate([prompt], params)[0] for prompt in prompts] ``` ``` # main, no hf_overrides Value error, Cannot find model module. 'Phi3VForCausalLM' is not a registered model in the Transformers library (only relevant if the model is meant to be in Transformers) and 'AutoModel' is not present in the model config's 'auto_map' (relevant if the model is custom). # main, hf_overrides INFO [model.py:788] Resolved architecture: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM # this PR, no hf_overrides INFO [registry.py:1436] Using Transformers' Phi3VModel for Phi3VForCausalLM. INFO [model.py:788] Resolved architecture: TransformersMultiModalForCausalLM ``` | prompt | prompt tokens | output (main with `hf_overrides` = this PR without) | |---|---|---| | [`pipeline-cat-chonk.jpeg`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/huggingface/documentation-images/resolve/main/pipeline-cat-chonk.jpeg) + "Describe this image in one sentence." | 774 | "A Pallas's cat is captured in mid-stride, walking on snow with a backdrop of snow-" | | "What is the capital of France?" | 15 | "The capital of France is Paris." | Token ids and logprobs are identical for every generated token.
## Details Decisions: - Is an info line enough, or should this warn? Without `trust_remote_code`, a checkpoint whose custom code reuses a Transformers config class now runs Transformers' class, as `AutoModel.from_pretrained` does without `trust_remote_code` and as main does when `architectures` is a Transformers class name (e.g. `Alibaba-NLP/gte-Qwen2-1.5B-instruct`: `Qwen2ForCausalLM` with a custom `AutoModel`). If the custom code changes the forward but keeps Transformers' parameter names, only the info line `Using Transformers' for .` shows the substitution. The same line is logged for the models above, which all have `AutoModel*` entries in `auto_map`, so a warning would fire for them too. If its weights differ, loading fails, e.g. `jinaai/jina-embeddings-v2-base-en` (`JinaBertForMaskedLM`, `model_type: bert`): "There is no module or parameter named 'model.encoder.layer.0.mlp' in TransformersForEmbedding". Trusted custom code still takes precedence, as discussed on #67732. - `model_impl="auto"` is left out, so architectures vLLM doesn't know still fail there as before ("are not supported for now", after warnings that ask for `trust_remote_code=True`). Extending the fallback to `auto` (dropping the `model_impl` condition) would make such custom-code checkpoints run Transformers' class by default.
Limitations - Other code still reads the Hub name in `architectures`: the runner and pooling-class defaults from its suffix in `_get_transformers_backend_cls`, the gpt-oss activation check in `moe.py`, class-keyed Transformers weight conversions in `_weight_conversions`, and `get_transformers_model_class` for MTP drafts. For the models above they give the same results as `model_impl="auto"` (or, for Phi-3-vision, as `hf_overrides`). - Rewriting `architectures` from `MODEL_MAPPING_NAMES`, as `get_config` does when the field is missing, would name the base model (`...Model`), and the suffix defaults would then pick the pooling runner. - The fallback comes before the `auto_map` loop because, without `trust_remote_code`, the loop can only fail, and it logs an "Unable to load ... `trust_remote_code=True`" traceback.

commits.pr_title: [Recipe] Kimi-K3.1-Pro: serve the model card's sampling defaults; Kimi-K3 / K3.1-Pro: opt-in strict tool calls
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Recipe-only change for Kimi-K3.1-Pro and Kimi-K3, from running the [Kimi Vendor Verifier](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier) suite on 8x MI355X (#66699, #65632). Kimi-K3.1-Pro now serves the model card's sampling values as server defaults, and both recipes get an opt-in "Strict tool calls" toggle. No Python or Rust code changes.

## Claims

- **Kimi-K3.1-Pro sampling defaults.** `base_args` gains `--override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95}'`. The checkpoint's `generation_config.json` holds only `max_length` and `eos_token_id`, so a request that omits `top_p` was sampled at vLLM's fallback 1.0, while the model card reports its results at temperature 1.0 and top-p 0.95. A value sent by the client still wins. The guide's curl example no longer sends `temperature: 0.7`.
- **Opt-in "Strict tool calls" toggle on Kimi-K3 and Kimi-K3.1-Pro.** It adds `--tool-strict-level parameter`. Without a grammar both models sometimes call a tool with empty or placeholder arguments. The default commands are unchanged.
- The toggle is not offered under `pd_cluster` (both recipes) or on TPU (K3.1 Pro).

## Validation

Model evaluation, 8x MI355X, single-node TP8, Python frontend:

| Model | Benchmark | Without | With | n |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Kimi-K3.1-Pro | KVV Tool Call, `--tool-strict-level parameter` | 0.786 (275/350) | 0.980 (343/350) | 70 samples x 5 epochs |
| Kimi-K3 | KVV Tool Call, `--tool-strict-level parameter` | 0.851 (298/350) | 0.983 (344/350) | 70 samples x 5 epochs |
| Kimi-K3.1-Pro | DeepSWE, agent sends no sampling parameters vs agent sends `temperature 1.0`, `top_p 0.95` | 0.664 (75/113) | 0.779 (88/113) | 113 tasks, one run each |

- K3.1 Pro numbers are on upstream main 8c17e4692a. K3 numbers are on a development build at main as of 2026-11-07 plus unrelated ROCm commits (v0.33.0rc1.dev1001).
- The K3.1 Pro strict run was one server start with both new flags (`--tool-strict-level parameter` and the override). At startup the server logged `{'temperature': 1.0, 'top_p': 0.95}` as its default sampling parameters, a chat request with no sampling parameters completed, and the server log has no 400 or 500 response for the run.
- **The DeepSWE pair set the values in the agent, not with the server flag.** DeepSWE was not re-run with the server-side form. What is verified for the flag is the startup log above and the parameter resolution below.
- DeepSWE details: paired exact McNemar p = 0.029 (22 tasks resolved only with top_p 0.95, 9 only without). Stray CJK tokens appeared in 55 of 113 tasks without and 1 with. Each configuration ran once, so run-to-run noise is not measured. In the top_p 0.95 run two agents were OOM-killed by the task harness and are counted as unresolved.

Checks run on this branch (CPU only):

```bash
# from a checkout of vllm-project/recipes@46e1415, as the Recipes PR check does
node scripts/validate-source.mjs --source vllm --dir <vllm>/recipes   # rc=0 on the base and on this branch
pre-commit run --from-ref origin/main --to-ref HEAD                     # 6 passed, 0 failed, 36 skipped (no matching files)
```

<details>
<summary>Rendered output, base vs this branch</summary>

- 41 published JSON files differ: 37 for Kimi-K3.1-Pro, plus the Kimi-K3 recipe JSON and its three promoted variants.
- Kimi-K3.1-Pro: all 249 rendered launch commands (81 `vllm serve`, 168 `python3 -m dynamo.vllm`) carry `--override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95}'` exactly once. The base has it 0 times.
- No published command contains `--tool-strict-level`; it appears only in the feature definition and the guides.
- With the toggle switched on for Kimi-K3.1-Pro, rendering every hardware profile, strategy, PD router, preset, preset point and frontend (954 renders) puts the flag exactly once on `vllm serve` for `single_node_tp`, `single_node_tep`, `multi_node_tp` and `multi_node_tep`, and never on a `pd_cluster` command (572 `vllm serve`, 200 `dynamo.vllm`), a `dynamo.vllm` command, or TPU.
- The same render for Kimi-K3: never on a `pd_cluster` command (632 `vllm serve`, 496 `dynamo.vllm`).
</details>

<details>
<summary>How the override resolves (no server)</summary>

`ModelConfig.get_diff_sampling_param()` on the local Kimi-K3.1-Pro checkpoint, then `ChatCompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()` and `CompletionRequest.to_sampling_params()`, run on this branch:

| Server flags | Request | temperature | top_p |
|---|---|---|---|
| none | nothing sent | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| `--override-generation-config '{"temperature":1.0,"top_p":0.95}'` | nothing sent | 1.0 | 0.95 |
| same | `top_p: 1.0` sent | 1.0 | 1.0 |
| same | `temperature: 0.6` sent | 0.6 | 0.95 |
| `--generation-config vllm` plus the override | nothing sent | 1.0 | 0.95 |

Chat and completions give the same result.
</details>

Not run:

- No GPU or server validation of this exact branch. The flags were run on the builds named above, with the recipe's base arguments and a subset of the MI355X preset's, not through the pinned Docker images.
- DeepSWE with the server-side flag.
- The Rust frontend, for either change. It is the builder's default frontend for Kimi-K3.
- Dynamo and SMG deployments. That Dynamo workers accept `--override-generation-config` and reject `--tool-strict-level` was read in the Dynamo source, not run.
- The site preview (`pnpm dev`).

## Details

**Why a server default.** Clients that leave sampling to the server get vLLM's fallback, not the card's values. The coding agent used for DeepSWE sends neither `temperature` nor `top_p` by default.

**Trade-offs of putting it in `base_args`.**

- Every Kimi-K3.1-Pro command gains the flag, including the benchmark-lane presets. Those lanes were measured without it. A client that sends `top_p` is unaffected; for one that does not, top-p filtering is now active, and its throughput cost was not measured.
- The model cards do not use 0.95 everywhere. The K3.1 Pro card says 0.95 unless specified and uses top-p 1.0 for BrowseComp. The K3 card uses 0.95 for single-step tasks and 1.0 for agentic tasks.
- The evidence for 0.95 on agentic work is one DeepSWE pair, one run each.
- Kimi-K3 is left alone: its checkpoint has the same two-key `generation_config.json`, but its card's agentic setting is top-p 1.0, which vLLM already serves, and there is no K3 measurement at 0.95.

**Why the strict toggle is opt-in.**

- Both measurements are on the Python frontend, one platform, one benchmark. The Rust frontend builds its own grammar and was not measured.
- With the flag, a tool schema the grammar cannot compile fails the whole request, also for tools that do not set `strict`. A `tool_choice="auto"` request that also sets `response_format` can return a tool call instead of the structured answer (related: #62499, #68251). Both were checked on the Python frontend.
- On Kimi-K3 the flag needs vLLM 0.31.0 (#56268) and the recipe's `min_vllm_version` stays 0.29.0; the feature description and the guide say so. Kimi-K3.1-Pro already requires 0.35.0.

**Why not under PD, and how it interacts with the Dynamo presets.** The builder passes feature args to `python3 -m dynamo.vllm` under the Dynamo router, and that worker parses engine arguments only. Each feature therefore has a `strategies` allowlist without `pd_cluster`, so the flag is never rendered there, for any router. The five Kimi-K3.1-Pro Dynamo presets are all `pd_cluster` and keep constraining tool calls through their own `--dyn-enable-structural-tag`; their commands change only by the sampling override. Cost: users of the native router under PD must add the flag by hand, and a strategy added to either recipe later does not get the toggle until it is added to the allowlist. The schema has no deny-list.

**TPU.** The K3.1 Pro toggle is marked unsupported on `ironwood`: the guide states that the tool-call parser was not exercised on TPU.

**Not a duplicate.** Searched open PRs on 2026-11-24 for `override-generation-config Kimi`, `Kimi-K3.1-Pro recipe`, `Kimi-K3 recipe`, `tool-strict-level`, `Kimi sampling top_p`, `generation_config Kimi`, `kimi_k3 strict`, `strict tool calls recipe`, and `66699` / `65632` in the body. No open PR adds sampling defaults or `--tool-strict-level` to a recipe, and neither issue has a comment about them. No recipe uses `--tool-strict-level` today; `--override-generation-config` has one precedent (`Google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it.yaml`).

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Migrate A.X-K1 to the Transformers modeling backend
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Migrate A.X-K1 (`AXK1ForCausalLM`) to the Transformers modeling backend and delete the native `AXK1.py`. Loading `skt/A.X-K1` needs huggingface/transformers#50644, so it requires Transformers 5.23.

Prerequisites:
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69868 (MoE fuser splice), so A.X-K1's MoE blocks fuse with `post_mlp_layernorm` kept
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67283 (ROCm AITER fused shared experts), which replaces native A.X-K1's fused shared experts
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69918 (ignored unexpected keys matched after renaming), so the dense layers' unused `post_mlp_layernorm` is skipped

## Claims

- A.X-K1 runs on the backend with LoRA and PP, matching native within noise and at least as fast.
- Native A.X-K1 cannot load the current `skt/A.X-K1` checkpoint (converted to fused experts on 2026-07-24), so nothing that works today is lost.

## Validation

B200, first 4 layers of `skt/A.X-K1` (native uses revision `5c7dc16b21`, the last with per-expert weights), greedy, 5 random-token prompts of 16-6000 tokens:

| Comparison | Greedy tokens | Max first-token logprob diff |
|---|---|---|
| Native eager vs native compiled (noise) | 39/40 | 0.25 |
| Backend vs native, compiled | 40/40 | 0.25 |
| Backend vs native, eager | 39/40 | 0.25 |
| Backend PP=2 vs native, eager | 39/40 | 0.18 |
| Backend vs native, both with a random r=8 LoRA (3 prompts) | 24/24 | 0.30 |

The LoRA changes the outputs of both (0-2/8 tokens match without it), so it is applied. The PP=2 and LoRA rows were run before the fuser change, which leaves the compiled outputs bit-identical.

| `vllm bench throughput` (1024 in / 256 out, 1000 prompts, 3 alternating rounds) | req/s (median) |
|---|---|
| Native (`main`) | 99.4 (98.3-103.6) |
| Backend (this PR) | 106.7 (106.7-110.5) |

The splice was also checked on every HF MoE block (tiny random configs from HF's testers): the same 48 of 60 blocks fuse as before, and each spliced forward matches HF's exactly on CPU. Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (shared expert with sigmoid gate) is within `main`'s run-to-run noise, eager and compiled.

```python
llm = LLM("axk1_4L", model_impl=impl, max_model_len=8192, enforce_eager=eager, seed=0)
llm.generate(prompts, SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=8, logprobs=5))
```
```bash
vllm bench throughput --model axk1_4L --input-len 1024 --output-len 256 --num-prompts 1000 --max-model-len 4096
```

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Attention] Enable ShardQ for SM90 FlashInfer NoPE sparse MLA prefill
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

On Hopper, GLM-5.3-Flash uses the FlashInfer FA3 sparse MLA backend. With TP8, the existing head-sharded path scores the same long-prefill query rows on all eight ranks. This PR connects that backend to the token split and collectives already merged in #63956. Each rank scores its own prefill rows and attends them with all heads. The existing decode path continues to partition by head.

The backend opts in for eligible NoPE prefills with BF16 or E4M3 KV (`fp8` and `fp8_e4m3`). Queries use BF16. The selected KV dtype and scale are shared by both paths. The rank-local FA3 plan shares the existing floating-point workspace. It reads compact Top-K rows after the decode prefix and uses the original query-row IDs to clamp per-work KV lengths on the GPU. The async planner reuses the CPU row split and sequence-length upper bounds.

**Related work.** #54394 exchanges indexer results. #67149 adds a fused scorer and Top-K selector. This patch applies directly to main. #67510 targets HiSparse host-backed KV and #68828 targets prefill context parallelism. #68301 changes dense-prefill routing in the same builder and may require a rebase.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_mla_sparse_sm90.py
```

For the BF16 KV serving comparisons below, use the same GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 weights on one 8 × H20 96 GB node. Both arms used BF16 with the default KV dtype (`auto`), TP8/DP1 and local vLLM KV caching. The engine selected `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM90` for 11 target-model layers.

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name GLM-5.3-Flash-indexer \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
  --max-model-len 512000 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-cache-retention-interval 0 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --moe-backend triton \
  --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune --trust-remote-code \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45
```

On the PR build, append `--attention-config '{"sparse_mla_shard_q":false}'` for the control and `--attention-config '{"sparse_mla_shard_q":true}'` for the candidate. Under the default settings on this checkpoint, splitting requires at least 1,024 new prefill tokens in the step and a prefill sequence-length upper bound above `index_topk` (2,048). For the mixed workload, also pass `--spec-method glm5_next_mtp --spec-tokens 3` to both arms. Single-request runs used no speculative decoding.

Send matched token IDs to `/v1/completions` with a fresh cache salt per request, temperature 0, `stream=true`, `return_token_ids=true` and `ignore_eos=true`. Measure TTFT at the first streamed output token ID and end-to-end latency at stream completion. Verify the input/output counts, stream completion, prefix-hit and preemption deltas.

## Test Result

**H20 backend tests.** The suite passed all 38 tests on H20. It covers both E4M3 aliases, BF16, the global opt-out and nonzero RoPE. The real FlashInfer regression checks noncontiguous query rows with E4M3 KV at scale 0.5 against the same stored values dequantized to BF16. The earlier BF16-only head passed 37 tests.

### Upstream serving comparison on 8 × H20

Both arms ran the same image built from the published PR runtime at `d456fa2d` and the official native binaries from its parent `ad905338`. Each configuration was restarted twice. The second comparison reversed the order of the two arms. Timing started after a warm-up of the corresponding workload. All 136 timed requests per arm completed with the expected token counts, zero prefix-cache hits and zero preemptions.

**Cold prefill, concurrency 1.** Four matched inputs per length and arm, with 256 output tokens each. Values are medians. Percent changes use the unrounded medians.

| Input tokens | TTFT off → on | TTFT reduction | End-to-end off → on | End-to-end reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 131,072 | 9.63 → 6.35 s | 34.08% | 11.02 → 7.74 s | 29.82% |
| 511,744 | 47.15 → 26.02 s | 44.81% | 48.53 → 27.40 s | 43.54% |

**Mixed prefill/decode, concurrency 32, MTP3.** Four measured bursts per arm. In every burst, one 131,072-token prompt started first. All 31 short prompts (1,024, 2,048 or 4,096 tokens) arrived before its first output token, starting at 350 ms and spaced 32 ms apart. Every request generated 128 tokens.

| Metric | ShardQ off | ShardQ on | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Short-request P95 TTFT | 13.48 s | 8.92 s | −33.80% |
| Long-request median TTFT | 10.17 s | 6.60 s | −35.16% |
| Short-request P95 TPOT | 38.71 ms | 32.00 ms | −17.34% |
| Aggregate output throughput | 256.08 tokens/s | 359.47 tokens/s | +40.38% |
| Accepted / proposed MTP tokens | 11,873 / 13,713 (86.58%) | 11,902 / 13,650 (87.19%) | +0.61 percentage points |

Throughput is total output tokens divided by summed active burst durations. The two restart pairs improved throughput by 40.71% and 40.04%. Short-request P95 covers 124 requests per arm. These measurements characterize bursts with an overlapping cold prefill.

**Correctness and capacity.** Both arms retrieved the planted phrase in 8/8 single requests and 4/4 mixed long requests. Mixed short requests retrieved it in 122/124 (off) and 123/124 (on). The first token matched for all 136 pairs. The complete greedy sequences matched in 61/136 pairs (1/8 single, 60/128 mixed). This retrieval check measures one aspect of model quality. Reported KV capacity fell by 0.55% without MTP (2,529,141 → 2,515,286 tokens) and 0.59% with MTP3 (2,104,263 → 2,091,760 tokens).

### Supplementary long-context quality check on the R5 integration

We scored the same 24 [OpenAI MRCR prompts at a fixed revision](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d) with ShardQ off and on in the same R5 integration candidate. There were eight prompts each at 2, 4 and 8 needles, spanning 70,478–104,029 rendered input tokens. GLM-5.3-Flash ran on 8 × H20, TP8, BF16 KV, MTP3, temperature 0, seed 42, natural EOS and a 2,048-token output cap. Each budget/flag combination had one independent engine start. Three Python modules were adapted to the R5 preallocated planner. All 13 checked vLLM native binaries matched the R5 baseline by SHA-256.

| Batched-token budget | Mean MRCR score /100, off → on | Per-prompt higher / equal / lower | Truncated, off → on | Empty final answer, off → on |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 89.26 → 95.86 | 6 / 18 / 0 | 3 → 1 | 2 → 0 |
| 32,768 | 88.57 → 92.06 | 3 / 20 / 1 | 3 → 1 | 2 → 1 |

This sample checks long-context quality in one integration. The 32,768 budget includes one lower-scoring answer. Output length limits and run-to-run generation variability matter, and the serving results above retain their original upstream baseline and exact-output caveats.

<!-- pr69086-fp8-evidence-begin -->
### FP8 E4M3 KV

Following the [FP8 review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69086#issuecomment-7139479408), eligible NoPE prefills also support ShardQ with ordinary E4M3 KV. For these comparisons both arms used `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`, differing only in `sparse_mla_shard_q`. All 11 target layers used the SM90 FlashInfer backend, with E4M3 KV observed on all eight TP ranks.

**Numerics and cold serving.** All 24 rank/scale checks passed against an FP32 reference (8 H20s, KV scales 0.5, 1 and 2). The largest relative L2 error with ShardQ was 0.255%. The candidate backend test file passed 38 tests. With MTP off, four matched cold prompts per length and 256 generated tokens per request, median end-to-end latency fell from 13.88 to 8.13 s at 131,072 input tokens (41.46%), and from 59.72 to 28.61 s at 511,744 (52.09%). Both restart orders gave the same direction. The eight GPUs recorded zero added software or hardware thermal-throttle time during these runs.

**Short-prefill routing.** On an H20 we exercised the real builder and planner as logical TP8 rank 0 with BF16 and E4M3 KV and with 0 or 3 speculative tokens. Eight cold 256-token inputs stayed on dense MHA both ways, with bitwise-equal dense forward outputs. At 2,048 tokens a single cold prefill still used dense MHA. At 2,049 it used sparse MQA both ways and only the enabled side split the query rows.

**GSM8K.** On 8 × H20 (TP8, 100-shot, same 1,319 questions), ShardQ off/on scored 1,216/1,319 and 1,214/1,319. The paired difference was −0.15 percentage points (95% interval −1.98 to +1.68). The [reviewer's independent H100 check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69086#issuecomment-7137418313) scored 94.53% in both arms on 128 questions.

**Long-context quality.** The same 24 [MRCR prompts](https://huggingface.co/datasets/openai/mrcr/tree/f4c69fae7cf81f7ca26b9fee34b392a50f6b8a1d) as above, 70,478–104,029 rendered tokens, were scored with the [pinned vLLM scorer](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d456fa2d1201a25c0003cbe95560c8a7002a3a42/tests/evals/mrcr/mrcr_eval.py). We fixed the batched-token budget at 8,192 and used greedy decoding, seed 42, `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false`, natural EOS, a 2,048-token cap, and MTP off. We then repeated all eight 8-needle items after independent engine restarts in reverse order. Both arms used identical rendered tokens for every pair.

| Sample | MRCR /100, off → on | Higher / equal / lower | Truncated, off → on | Empty answer, off → on |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 prompts | 82.82 → 91.04 | 3 / 21 / 0 | 4 → 2 | 4 → 2 |
| 8 needles (first pass) | 62.31 → 74.53 | 1 / 7 / 0 | 3 → 2 | 3 → 2 |
| 8 needles (reverse repeat) | 74.53 → 64.01 | 1 / 6 / 1 | 2 → 3 | 2 → 1 |

The headline score includes all prompts and capped responses. Repeating the 8-needle set within each configuration changed the mean by +12.22 points (off) and -10.52 points (on). Run-to-run variation on these items limits conclusions about general FP8 quality parity.

Both arms reached natural EOS on 20/24 prompts. Their paired mean score changed by +0.065 points on those prompts. Across the full set, 2 responses changed from empty to nonempty and 0 went the other way. The largest drop in the reverse repeat was 99.46 → 5.56 on one 8-needle prompt (finish reasons `stop` → `length`).

As a post-hoc cap sensitivity check, we repeated all 5 prompts that hit the length cap in any of the four runs, with 4,096 output tokens allowed. We ran on then off with one fresh start per arm. Scores (off → on) were 50.84 → 86.36/100, with 0 → 0 capped responses and 0 → 0 empty answers. This selected subset is reported separately from the primary score. One item reached natural EOS in both arms and scored 97.78 → 36.60.

<details>
<summary>Frozen MRCR sample IDs</summary>

For each needle count N, use shard `Nneedle/Nneedle_1.parquet` from the dataset revision linked above. The zero-based positions below refer to the stream after `shuffle(seed=42+N, buffer_size=16)`. These IDs were fixed in the earlier BF16 evaluation.

- 2 needles — `193, 195, 196, 197, 203, 204, 205, 208`
- 4 needles — `192, 194, 195, 196, 197, 204, 207, 208`
- 8 needles — `192, 193, 194, 196, 202, 203, 204, 205`

</details>
<!-- pr69086-fp8-evidence-end -->

<details>
<summary>Earlier serving-build benchmarks and backend correctness checks</summary>

**Backend correctness.** On an H20, all **31 tests passed** with the Python sources from `2f170a0fed20` plus this patch and the compiled dependencies from the serving image. Against the unpatched sources, the four new cases failed and the 27 existing cases passed. The new cases cover compact Top-K offsets, pure and mixed prefill planning, and GPU clamping for noncontiguous query rows. The four source files have identical contents at that test base and at the PR parent `ad9053380fe8`.

**Serving latency.** Single node, 8 × H20 96 GB. We measured the equivalent patch on the serving build (`0.34.0rc1.dev1004+g5020556c3.generic.r5`), preserving that build's plan chunking. Each input length had six matched cold prompts across two separate service launches per arm. Every timed request produced 256 tokens, with zero prefix hits and zero preemptions. Times are medians in seconds. Percent reductions are medians of paired per-prompt reductions.

| Input tokens | Control TTFT | ShardQ TTFT | TTFT reduction | Control end-to-end | ShardQ end-to-end | End-to-end reduction |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 131,072 | 9.59 s | 6.31 s | 34.27% | 10.98 s | 7.68 s | 29.99% |
| 393,216 | 33.77 s | 19.65 s | 41.80% | 35.14 s | 21.02 s | 40.18% |
| 511,744 | 47.04 s | 25.93 s | 44.86% | 48.40 s | 27.29 s | 43.62% |

A separate control restart on nine repeated prompts gave a median end-to-end change below 0.07% at every length.

- **Numerical and model checks.** In two captured GLM indexer shapes, all 4,480 TP8 Top-512 row sets matched the reference, with maximum relative L2 error of 0.00118 for the full attention subgraph. In serving, both arms retrieved the planted two-word answer within the first 64 generated tokens on 18/18 prompts. First tokens matched on 18/18 pairs. All 256 greedy token IDs matched on 7/18 pairs. Control versus control across restarts matched on 2/9 full sequences. The retrieval metric checks the planted answer and does not establish broad model parity.
- **Mixed batches and capacity.** Two overlapping requests (8,192 input / 512 output and 32,768 input / 128 output) completed, with mixed prefill/decode steps observed and zero preemptions. Per-GPU KV allocation fell from 33.37 to 33.22 GiB. Reported KV capacity dropped from 2,531,660 to 2,517,805 tokens (0.55%).
- **Scope.** The earlier serving-build table covers single-request latency. The upstream run above adds MTP3 and burst concurrency. The separate E4M3 results above cover single-request cold prefill. Steady-state load and other models remain outside the serving evaluation.

</details>

AI assistance was used for implementation, experiment analysis, and drafting this description. The submitting author reviewed the changes line by line and ran the relevant tests.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Remove TeleFLM
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Remove `TeleFLMForCausalLM` support completely from vLLM, as `TeleFLMForCausalLM` does not exist in upstream Transformers and its remote code is incompatible with Transformers 5.x. v0.34.0 is the last release that supports it. Updates this PR per maintainer review and relates to #67937.

Duplicate-work check: `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "teleflm"` and `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state open --search "67937 in:body"` showed no other open PR removing or modifying TeleFLM.

## Claims

- Delete `vllm/model_executor/models/teleflm.py` (45 lines) and remove `"TeleFLMForCausalLM"` from `_TEXT_GENERATION_MODELS` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py`.
- Add `"TeleFLMForCausalLM": "0.34.0"` to `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS` in `vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py` so loading `TeleFLMForCausalLM` raises the versioned deprecation `ValueError`.
- Remove `"TeleFLMForCausalLM"` from `tests/models/registry.py` and `docs/models/supported_models.md`.
- Delete `examples/template_teleflm.jinja` and its parametrization entry in `tests/renderers/test_hf.py`.

## Validation

All checks below ran on commit `e7067421a0713c169a3a074233e50a445fe9bb43` (based on `upstream/main` `aec644a8f9`) on macOS CPU (Python 3.12.15, `transformers 5.22.2`).

### Local CPU pytest results (filtered)

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "test_hf_registry_coverage or test_lazy_modelinfo or test_weight_utils_atomic_writer_reexport or test_fill_model_info_cache or (test_registry_model_property and not Llava and not Step5) or (test_registry_is_pp and not Qwen2VL) or (test_registry_supports_hc_sp and not Qwen4Exp) or test_registry_may_use_target_embed or (test_registry_supports_replayssm and not NemotronH_Nano and not NemotronH_Omni and not Qwen3_5)" -v
# ========== 22 passed, 3 skipped, 451 deselected, 1 warning in 26.07s ===========

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "TeleFLM or test_hf_registry_coverage" -v
# ================= 1 passed, 475 deselected, 1 warning in 1.41s =================

.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/renderers/test_hf.py -k "not test_resolve_content_format_examples and not test_resolve_content_format_hf_defined and not test_get_gen_prompt" -v
# =========== 44 passed, 6 failed, 28 deselected, 1 warning in 49.35s ============
```

Local coverage limitation: the macOS CPU environment lacks `torchvision` and an `HF_TOKEN` for gated repos, so `test_resolve_content_format_examples` (which loads `Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct`), vision-model cases in `test_registry.py`, and `google/paligemma-3b-mix-224` in `test_hf.py` fail locally and rely on Linux CI for full execution. To cover the `tests/renderers/test_hf.py` edit locally, we verified with `load_chat_template` and `_try_extract_ast` that all 7 remaining `examples/template_*.jinja` files load and parse cleanly.

### Real `ModelConfig` deprecation check and pre-commit

<details>
<summary>Deprecation probe and pre-commit output on commit e7067421a0713c169a3a074233e50a445fe9bb43</summary>

```text
Verified 7 remaining example templates load and parse AST
```

`pre-commit run` passed on all staged files (`ruff check`, `ruff format`, `typos`, `markdownlint-cli2`, `check-test-tethering`, `mypy`, `check-spdx-headers`, `check-root-lazy-imports`, `check-forbidden-strings`, `check-docstring-style`, `check-trust-remote-code`, and `signoff-commit`).

</details>

## Details

- Adding `"TeleFLMForCausalLM": "0.34.0"` to `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS` matches recent model removals (PR #67035 and PR #68177) against the latest release (`v0.34.0`).
- Preexisting registry resolution note: in `ModelRegistry.resolve_model_cls`, `_try_resolve_transformers` runs before `_raise_for_unsupported`. When a checkpoint omits `trust_remote_code=True` (`CofeAI/FLM-2-52B-Instruct-2407`), `HFConfigParser.parse` prompts for `trust_remote_code=True`; when `trust_remote_code=True` is passed on `CofeAI/FLM-2-52B-Instruct-2407`, remote `modeling_teleflm.py` fails backend compatibility and falls through to the `_PREVIOUSLY_SUPPORTED_MODELS` error.

commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Splice the fused MoE into the MoE block's traced forward
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`MoEBlockFuser` now splices vLLM's fused MoE into the MoE block's traced forward instead of replacing the whole forward, so blocks with extra modules around the experts can fuse. Split out of https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67277 (A.X-K1, whose MoE block ends in `post_mlp_layernorm`), which needs it.

## Claims

- Only the experts call (plus the scale and shared expert the fused MoE applies) is replaced; the rest of the block runs as traced, e.g. a norm after the experts or a projection before them.
- The fuser fails closed when the trace cannot stand in for the forward: optional inputs, leaf calls, tensor constants, the experts' output or moved modules used elsewhere, or a trace specialized on the sequence length.
- Fusers trace in eval mode, so training-only branches (Mixtral's router jitter) are never baked in.
- The experts' scale must equal `routed_scaling_factor`; this replaces `divides_shared_output`, which the backend never set because it never selects `RoutedScaleMode.OUTPUT_FP16_GUARD`.

## Validation

Run on https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/67277 at c01dcd44f5, whose fuser code is the same as this PR's apart from changes merged on `main` since:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Every HF MoE block (tiny random configs from HF's testers) | Same 48 of 60 blocks fuse as on `main`; each spliced forward matches HF's exactly on CPU |
| Qwen1.5-MoE-A2.7B (shared expert with sigmoid gate), eager and compiled | Within `main`'s run-to-run noise |
| A.X-K1 (first 4 layers), backend vs native, compiled | 40/40 greedy tokens, compiled outputs bit-identical before and after the splice |

`pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_moe.py` on 90fad70b56: 40 passed in 7.31s.

commits.pr_title: [Model] Decouple `nemotron_nas` from llama
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Decouple `vllm/model_executor/models/nemotron_nas.py` from `llama.py` by inlining `DeciLMMLP` and `DeciLMAttention`. Part of #67937.

## Claims

- Removes all `vllm.model_executor.models.llama` imports from `nemotron_nas.py`. Parameter names and weight loading are unchanged.
- `DeciLMMLP` matches `LlamaMLP` (keeps `bias` and `maybe_fused_act_quant`). It drops `reduce_results`/`disable_tp`, which `nemotron_nas` never passed.
- `DeciLMAttention` matches `LlamaAttention` plus the previous `_init_rotary_emb` override (`mistral_yarn`/`rope_llama4` → `is_neox_style=False`), and keeps `layer_types` sliding-window support. It drops the Eagle3 draft `target_layer_count` offset, the `EncoderOnlyAttention` branch and the `attn_type` parameter, none of which DeciLM can reach.
- No open PR duplicates this (`gh pr list --state open` for `nemotron_nas`, `DeciLM`). The open PR #68289 only adds EAGLE-3 aux hidden states.

## Validation

Run on 2x RTX 4090 (CUDA 13.2, PyTorch `2.14.0+cu132`, Python `3.14.10`) against base `850fd21d75`, before the `domyn_edge.py` changes were split out:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_registry.py -k "DeciLM or DomynEdge" -v
# 2 passed, 472 deselected in 3.71s
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/test_initialization.py -k "DeciLMForCausalLM or DomynEdgeForCausalLM" -v
# 2 passed, 447 deselected, 2 warnings in 41.30s
```

- `nvidia/Llama-3_3-Nemotron-Super-49B-v1` (4 layers, seeded random weights, `enforce_eager=True`, greedy, 16 tokens): prompt logprobs, greedy tokens and output logprobs are bitwise identical to `main`.
- `tests/models/test_pp_equivalence.py::_check_equivalent(VllmRunner, "DeciLMForCausalLM", 2)`: bitwise equivalent at `PP=1` vs `PP=2`.
- `DeciLMMLP(bias=False/True)` matches `LlamaMLP` bit-exactly on CUDA `bfloat16`.

Since then, the only code change is removing the unused `attn_type` parameter. `Attention` already defaults to `AttentionType.DECODER`, so behaviour is unchanged. Pre-commit passes.

AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Frontend] Report time to first content token in per-request metrics
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds optional `time_to_first_content_token_ms` to Python and Rust frontend per-request metrics for streaming Chat Completions, Completions, and Responses. Addresses #54829; extends the existing metrics from #46768 and #55084 rather than introducing another metrics API.

## Claims

- Measures from request scheduling to the first engine output batch that produces non-empty text content, excluding reasoning and tool calls.
- Both frontends observe content directly: no parser-configuration timing flag or TTFT fallback. No text means no TTFC; it equals TTFT when the first output batch produces text.
- Uses the existing `--enable-per-request-metrics` flag. Existing aggregate metrics, speculative-decoding metrics, and attribution/suppression rules are unchanged.
- Streaming metrics appear on the final usage chunk for Chat Completions/Completions and the terminal Responses event. Non-streaming TTFC remains `null`.

## Validation

Validated implementation: `2ad8dacfaa`, based on CI bot merge `18803b55c3fb`.

| Local validation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Python component tests | 181 passed, 1 existing xfail; 4 focused Chat tests passed |
| Rust chat/server/text libraries | 1405 passed, 1 existing ignored test |
| A100: Qwen2.5 + Qwen3, shared E2E | Python 5 passed; Rust 5 passed |
| A100: empty output, tool-choice on/off | Both frontends passed all 3 endpoints with either switch setting |
| A100: gpt-oss-20b, Harmony | Python 6 cases passed; Rust 6 cases passed |

Changed-file pre-commit and Rust Clippy checks passed. This is correctness validation, not a performance benchmark; upstream CI must validate the final head.

<details>
<summary>Commands and evidence</summary>

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_protocol.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/responses/test_serving_responses.py \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/completion/test_completion_error.py -q
# 181 passed, 1 xfailed, 14 warnings in 35.09s

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_serving_chat.py \
  -q -k 'per_request or timing_metrics or streaming_metrics'
# 4 passed, 222 deselected, 14 warnings in 2.52s

# Run the following against each frontend. Rust additionally sets
# VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1 and VLLM_RUST_FRONTEND_PATH to the rebuilt binary.
VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py::test_per_request_metrics_non_streaming \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_chat_completion.py::test_per_request_metrics_on_final_usage_chunk \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/chat_completion/test_thinking_token_budget.py::test_thinking_token_budget_limits_reasoning_with_metrics -q -s
# Python: 5 passed, 14 warnings in 83.21s (0:01:23)
# Rust:   5 passed, 14 warnings in 74.47s (0:01:14)
```

These use real Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen3-0.6B weights on one A100 80GB, through the existing `RemoteOpenAIServer` fixtures. Qwen3 covers explicit and automatic reasoning configuration. The existing final-usage test now also covers EOS-only output. Restoring the previous Chat TTFT fallback makes that EOS row fail: `1 failed, 14 warnings in 54.21s`; after the fix it passes in both frontend runs above. No new test functions were added.

```bash
# From rust/. cargo-nextest is not installed locally.
CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
  cargo test -p vllm-chat -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --lib -j 8
# chat:   538 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 3.69s
# server: 733 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 18.20s
# text:   134 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored; finished in 2.13s

CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=0 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 \
  cargo clippy -p vllm-chat -p vllm-text -p vllm-server --all-targets -j 8 -- -D warnings
```

Local validation uses Python 3.12, Torch 2.13/cu130, existing precompiled native extensions, and a newly built Rust binary. It is not a fully synchronized CI dependency installation. An overly broad local selection of `test_serving_chat.py` also selected unrelated gpt-oss GPU fixtures and hit a missing FlashInfer import during server initialization; those errors were not counted as passing component tests. The focused selection above passed.

</details>

## Details

For reasoning workloads, the first generated token can precede text content substantially. The new field supports per-request content-start latency monitoring, reasoning-effort analysis, and model comparisons. Average TPOT and token counts cannot reconstruct the observed boundary; client arrival times also include transport and buffering.

Both frontends reuse existing parser/decoder output without a second parsing pass. Tracking actual content avoids differences caused by parser configuration or tool-choice switches. Empty, reasoning-only, and tool-only streams leave TTFC unset; echoed prompts do not count as generated content. Available timestamps have engine output-batch resolution.

This measures the first text content in the current response, not the final answer across an entire multi-turn tool workflow. Existing aggregate example values are unchanged.

In Rust, adding the timestamp triggered Clippy's `large_enum_variant` lint on `AssistantEvent`. The existing spec-decoding `Box` allocation is moved from structured event assembly to `AssistantEvent::Done` construction to reduce the enum size; allocation count, metric values, and API serialization are unchanged.

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests, documentation, and review. The human submitter is responsible for reviewing and understanding the final diff.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoRIIO] Skip zeroing READ destinations and wait for their pending copies
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With a mixed-precision KV cache (e.g. DeepSeek-V4) and async scheduling, MoRIIO READ mode can lose prompt KV it has already received, as the model runner zeroes new blocks on the compute stream and nothing orders MoRI's writes after that. This PR leaves the blocks that a READ overwrites in full out of that zeroing, and makes the decode worker wait for the compute stream before its first read only when that stream still has block copies queued for the step's READ destinations.



## Claims

- READ destinations are not zeroed, and received KV is written only after the compute stream has finished copying into the destination blocks.
- That fixes the accuracy drop. On MI355X with MoRIIO READ over xGMI and async scheduling, DeepSeek-V4-Flash (P TP4 → D TP4) goes from 0.600 / 0.644 on main to 0.954 / 0.954 in GSM8K (strict-match / flexible-extract), against 0.955 / 0.955 without a connector. Qwen3-32B with an fp8 KV cache and layer 0 kept in bf16 (P TP1 → D TP1) goes from 0.056 / 0.064 to 0.923 / 0.905 over xGMI and from 0.036 / 0.036 to 0.934 / 0.918 over RDMA, against 0.927 / 0.918 without a connector.
- READ steps do not wait for zeroing. A step waits in two cases only, when a block copy or a hybrid Mamba state copy on the compute stream writes into a READ destination. The wait is a host sync with the compute stream, so under async scheduling such a step also waits for the previous step’s forward and loses the overlap. The READ steps of a mixed-precision model do not wait, and in the 8k/512 benchmark below throughput, TTFT, TPOT and ITL stay within 0.3% of main. At 16k/16, requests/s and TTFT stay within 0.2% and TPOT p50 within 0.13 ms.
- The destinations of a failed READ are zeroed in the next step, before `kv_load_failure_policy=recompute` recomputes into them.
- Other setups still work, such as no async scheduling, with a single-precision KV cache, or a hybrid Mamba model with prefix caching.



## Validation

### Unit tests

The new tests drive `start_load_kv` with a stream that records what gets called, they build each step's metadata from real KV cache groups, and they pass a failed read's report from the worker to the scheduler.

| What's tested | Tests | Main | With this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| The worker syncs the compute stream before the first read of a flagged step | `test_read_step_waits_for_compute_stream_before_first_read` | 1 failed | 1 passed |
| READ destinations are not zeroed, and local tail blocks that no read writes still are | `test_update_state_drops_decode_recompute_tail_block` (16 cases) | 2 failed, 14 passed | 16 passed |
| A step is flagged when a READ destination is copied, or when a hybrid Mamba state copy writes it | `test_read_meta_orders_reads_after_stream_work` (1 case), `test_hybrid_read_waits_only_when_state_is_copied_into_its_destination` (2 cases) | 3 failed | 3 passed |
| The destinations of a failed READ are zeroed in the next step | `test_failed_read_destinations_are_zeroed_in_the_next_step` (2 cases), `test_failed_read_destination_reused_by_a_read_is_not_zeroed`, `test_failed_read_returns_its_unzeroed_destinations_once`, `test_unzeroed_destinations_of_every_rank_are_merged` | 5 failed | 5 passed |
| Any other step isn't flagged, and unflagged steps, WRITE consumers and producers post without waiting | 9 more cases of those two tests, 3 more tests | 12 passed | 12 passed |


### End-to-end verification

All runs use one MI355X node with MoRIIO READ through the example moriio proxy, over xGMI unless the row says RDMA, `transfer_timeout` 2 s and FULL CUDA graphs (FULL_DECODE_ONLY for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B). The RDMA row reads through same-NIC loopback, with `MORI_RDMA_DEVICES` set to the prefill GPU's NIC on both instances. GSM8K sets 64 concurrent requests, 20-shot for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and 5-shot for Qwen3-32B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. DeepSeek-V4-Flash's prefill instance caps batches at 2,048 tokens, because the longer 20-shot prompts otherwise exhaust memory in the sparse-attention indexer. Cells show lm_eval (strict-match / flexible-extract) scores, and the baseline is the same model without a connector at the decode TP.

| Model, P → D | Configuration | Main | This PR | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 → TP4 | async scheduling | 0.600 / 0.644 | 0.954 / 0.954 | 0.955 / 0.955 |
| | async scheduling, prefix caching | 0.660 / 0.691 | 0.955 / 0.955 | 0.955 / 0.955 |
| | no async scheduling | 0.952 / 0.952 | 0.955 / 0.955 | 0.955 / 0.955 |
| Qwen3-32B, TP1 → TP1, fp8 KV, layer 0 bf16 | async scheduling | 0.056 / 0.064 | 0.923 / 0.905 | 0.927 / 0.918 |
| | async scheduling, RDMA | 0.036 / 0.036 | 0.934 / 0.918 | 0.927 / 0.918 |
| | no async scheduling | 0.929 / 0.908 | 0.926 / 0.904 | 0.927 / 0.918 |
| Qwen3-32B, TP1 → TP1, all layers fp8 (no zeroing) | async scheduling | 0.922 / 0.912 | 0.923 / 0.914 | 0.927 / 0.918 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (hybrid), TP1 → TP1 | async scheduling, prefix caching | 0.951 / 0.949 | 0.958 / 0.957 | 0.958 / 0.958 |

Every run completed all 1,319 requests with no errors, and decode received its prompt KV through the connector. Main loses accuracy only when blocks are zeroed and async scheduling is on.


### Benchmarks

Overhead is measured on Qwen3-32B with mixed-precision KV and async scheduling, where main zeroes the destinations of every READ step, and 1P1D both TP1.

ISL/OSL=8k/512 with concurrency 32 and 256 prompts per run.

| Metric | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 617.9 | 618.4 |
| Requests/s | 1.209 | 1.210 |
| TTFT p50 (ms) | 8,936 | 8,957 |
| TTFT p99 (ms) | 23,438 | 23,473 |
| TPOT p50 (ms) | 31.22 | 31.15 |
| TPOT p99 (ms) | 31.35 | 31.27 |
| ITL p50 (ms) | 30.45 | 30.38 |
| ITL p99 (ms) | 60.55 | 60.58 |

ISL/OSL=16k/16

| Concurrency | Metric | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 (96 prompts) | Requests/s | 0.4561 | 0.4558 |
| | TTFT p50 (ms) | 17,334 | 17,319 |
| | TTFT p99 (ms) | 17,568 | 17,546 |
| | TPOT p50 (ms) | 12.77 | 12.64 |
| 16 (192 prompts) | Requests/s | 0.4567 | 0.4567 |
| | TTFT p50 (ms) | 34,836 | 34,827 |
| | TTFT p99 (ms) | 34,940 | 34,923 |
| | TPOT p50 (ms) | 12.71 | 12.77 |

<details>
<summary>commands</summary>


```bash
HOST_IP=<node IP>
P_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_producer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8100", "handshake_port": "8104", "notify_port": "8120", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'
D_KV='{"kv_connector": "MoRIIOConnector", "kv_role": "kv_consumer", "kv_connector_extra_config": {"proxy_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "proxy_ping_port": "8001", "http_port": "8200", "handshake_port": "8204", "notify_port": "8220", "host_ip": "'$HOST_IP'", "backend": "xgmi", "read_mode": true, "transfer_timeout": 2}}'

python3 examples/disaggregated/disaggregated_serving/moriio_toy_proxy_server.py --port 8000 --service-discovery-port 8001

# DeepSeek-V4-Flash with P on GPUs 0-3 and D on GPUs 4-7. Each instance lists the other's GPUs after its own,
# so that MoRI can reach the peer's memory over xGMI.
DSV4='deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"} --trust-remote-code'
# async scheduling
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8100 --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8200 --async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# async scheduling, prefix caching
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8100 --async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8200 --async-scheduling --enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# no async scheduling
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8100 --no-async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching --max-num-batched-tokens 2048 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=4,5,6,7,0,1,2,3 vllm serve $DSV4 --port 8200 --no-async-scheduling --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"

# Qwen3-32B with P on GPU 0 and D on GPU 1
QWEN='Qwen/Qwen3-32B --tensor-parallel-size 1 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL"} --no-enable-prefix-caching --kv-cache-dtype fp8'
# fp8 KV, layer 0 bf16, async scheduling (also the benchmark setup)
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8100 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 0 --async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8200 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 0 --async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# the same over RDMA: "backend": "rdma" in P_KV and D_KV, and MORI_RDMA_DEVICES=<NIC of GPU 0> for both instances
# fp8 KV, layer 0 bf16, no async scheduling
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8100 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 0 --no-async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8200 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 0 --no-async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"
# all layers fp8, async scheduling
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8100 --async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve $QWEN --port 8200 --async-scheduling --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"

# Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with P on GPU 0 and D on GPU 1, async scheduling, prefix caching
HYBRID='Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --tensor-parallel-size 1 --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN --compilation-config {"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY"} --enable-prefix-caching --async-scheduling'
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 vllm serve $HYBRID --port 8100 --kv-transfer-config "$P_KV"
VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1,0 vllm serve $HYBRID --port 8200 --kv-transfer-config "$D_KV"

# baselines, without a connector
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 --port 8300 --tensor-parallel-size 4 --trust-remote-code
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-32B --port 8300 --tensor-parallel-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --port 8300 --tensor-parallel-size 1

# GSM8K on all 1,319 questions, with PORT=8000 (the proxy) for P/D and 8300 for the baselines
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 20 --seed 0 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 \
  --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731,base_url=http://$HOST_IP:$PORT/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=1,tokenized_requests=False,timeout=3600
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --seed 0 --gen_kwargs max_gen_toks=1024 \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B,base_url=http://$HOST_IP:$PORT/v1/completions,num_concurrent=64,max_retries=1,tokenized_requests=False,timeout=3600

# benchmarks, through the proxy
BENCH="vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --base-url http://$HOST_IP:8000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen3-32B --tokenizer Qwen/Qwen3-32B --dataset-name random --ignore-eos \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99"
# 8,192 input / 512 output tokens, a warm-up and then 3 runs
$BENCH --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 --seed 0 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 8
for s in 1 2 3; do $BENCH --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 512 --seed $s --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 32; done
# 16,384 input / 16 output tokens, in each session a warm-up and then 3 runs at each concurrency
$BENCH --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 16 --seed 0 --num-prompts 8 --max-concurrency 8
for s in 1 2 3; do $BENCH --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 16 --seed $s --num-prompts 96 --max-concurrency 8; done
for s in 101 102 103; do $BENCH --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 16 --seed $s --num-prompts 192 --max-concurrency 16; done

pytest -v tests/v1/kv_connector/unit -k moriio
```

</details>



## Details

In READ mode, `MoRIIOConnectorWorker.start_load_kv` posts MoRI reads into the request's new blocks right before the forward pass. Those blocks are also zeroed when `KVCacheConfig.needs_kv_cache_zeroing` is set (Mamba layers or mixed-precision attention caches), since core skips zeroing only for async loads and that MoRIIO READ is synchronous. `GPUModelRunner.update_requests` queues the zero kernel and any block copies on the compute stream before it calls `start_load_kv`, and for a hybrid Mamba model with prefix caching `MambaHybridModelState.preprocess_state` queues a state copy there too. MoRI writes from its own streams (xGMI) or from the NIC (RDMA), so nothing orders the reads after that work. With async scheduling, the zero kernel can still be queued behind the previous forward when the data lands, and it overwrites the received KV. No error is raised, and accuracy drops.

DeepSeek-V4 has a mixed-precision KV cache, with `fp8_ds_mla` main KV (the `auto` default), an fp8 indexer key cache and an fp32 compressor state. Qwen3-32B is made mixed with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --kv-cache-dtype-skip-layers 0` (layer 0 in bf16), which reproduces the issue. With all layers in fp8, nothing is zeroed and main passes.

The change contains the following parts:
- `build_connector_meta` removes the step's READ destinations from `new_block_ids_to_zero`, through the exception that `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_connector_meta` documents for synchronous READ connectors. #59164 did this for hybrid Mamba models, and doing it for every model follows the approach proposed in #62313 by benenzhu.
- `build_connector_meta` sets `MoRIIOConnectorMetadata.order_reads_after_compute_stream` on a step with a synchronous load when a READ destination is copied, or when a hybrid Mamba READ's scheduled tokens cross a Mamba block boundary, where the model runner copies the running state into the block that the READ fills (the scheduler output does not list Mamba state copies). Other steps are unchanged.
- On a flagged step, `start_load_kv` synchronizes the current stream once, after the handshake and before the first read. The sync runs inside `gpu_sync_allowed()` because `execute_model` runs under `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK`.
- A failed READ returns its destinations that skipped zeroing through `build_connector_worker_meta`, and the scheduler adds them to the next step's `new_block_ids_to_zero`. The exception in `KVConnectorBase_V1.build_connector_meta` asks to fail the step on a failed load, which would turn every failed READ into an engine failure, so its text is extended to allow this as well.

The wait is on the host because MoRI does not take a stream or event to wait on. Skipping zeroing for READ destinations is safe because the reads overwrite every head and token slot of every destination block. Each decode rank copies its whole shard of every layer of the block's cache group, cache groups that are not transferred have no READ destinations, and local blocks without a prefill counterpart, such as the tail for the recomputed last token, are not READ destinations and stay zeroed.

AI assistant was used in this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Nemotron Shortcut] Fix refits and match training video preprocessing
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Fix Nemotron Shortcut's bucketed refits and make video preprocessing match the training format. Still-image sizes continue to come from the checkpoint's HF processor, with explicit overrides preserved.

## Why and how

**Bucketed refits:** after the sparse model has loaded its indexer, a later weight bucket containing only attention or MLP weights is incorrectly rejected for having no indexer weights. Remember successful initial validation across subsequent buckets. An initial sparse checkpoint without indexer weights is still rejected.

**T=1 video prompts:** individually encoded frames currently bypass the timestamp-aware path used by T=2 tubelets. Reuse that path for both, preserving frame labels, loader metadata, frame caps, and processor-cache keys. Encode replacement segments separately so chat-tokenization merges cannot erase the visual placeholder range.

**Video frame sizes:** training uses different resize rules for still images and video frames. Still images preserve their aspect ratio within an image-size limit. Video frames instead use a separate patch budget; the default training configuration resizes each frame to a 448×448 square.

vLLM currently applies the still-image rule to video frames too. For example, with a 1036px image limit, a 1280×720 video frame is served as 1036×588 instead of the 448×448 square used during training:

| | Current vLLM | Training / with this fix |
|---|---|---|
| Resized frame | 1036×588 | 448×448 |
| Vision patches (14px each) | 74×42 = 3,108 | 32×32 = 1,024 |
| Visual embeddings at T=1, after 2×2 spatial merging | 777 | 256 |

The model therefore receives a different spatial layout and roughly three times as many visual embeddings, consuming more context than the training format.

The fix sizes video frames from the checkpoint's `video_target_num_patches` and `video_maintain_aspect_ratio` fields. Missing fields use the training defaults: 1024 vision patches and no aspect-ratio preservation, giving the 448×448 square with 14px patches. Apply this resize before grouping frames into T=1 or T=2 tubelets, using the training pixel transform: FP32 rescaling, OpenCV area interpolation, then normalization. Still-image resizing keeps its existing checkpoint settings and overrides.

Memory profiling uses this same video geometry. Aspect-preserving frame shapes that exceed the profiled patch budget are rejected.

Main already reads still-image sizes through the HF processor. Regression tests preserve that behavior for different checkpoint sizes and both engine-level and per-request overrides.

## Validation

The same processor tests were run against main revision `9d91dd2a95d1` and the preprocessing update:

```bash
OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/models/nemotron_shortcut/test_video_processing.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/models/nemotron_shortcut -q
```

```text
base: 9 failed, 6 passed, 1 warning in 13.95s
PR:   15 passed, 1 warning in 59.77s
```

The tests cover timestamps/caching, loader labels and caps, chat boundaries, T=1/T=2 frame sizes, exact normalized pixels, HWC/CHW inputs, profiling bounds, and checkpoint image sizes/overrides. The warning is the unbuilt checkout's missing version module.

Four GB300 LLM serving smoke checks passed with a tiny dummy-weight model: checkpoint image size, explicit image-size override, HWC video, and CHW video. Each checked visual-token counts and successful one-token generation.

The corrected TP2 refit regression passed in [B200 CI](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/105762#01a21360-308c-47a3-8381-ee31a49e30c4), together with the full Nemotron Shortcut suite:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/nemotron_shortcut/ -v -s
```

```text
182 passed, 2 skipped, 428 warnings in 411.48s (0:06:51)
```

Full pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` pass. The TP2 refit regression loads an indexer bucket, a replicated normalization-weight bucket, and an empty bucket, checking that the parameter values are preserved. The normalization weight has the full checkpoint shape on each rank; a TP-local packed QKV shard does not. Full benchmark accuracy has not been re-evaluated; video token counts change intentionally to match training.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Kimi K3] Specialized decode: compile each kernel once, only for captured sizes
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Cuts the NVIDIA Kimi-K3 specialized decode's (`decode_backend=latency_specialized`) startup compiles by about 2/3 by not compiling kernels that are never used: on 8x B300 (Kimi-K3.1-Pro, `--max-num-seqs 64`), CuTe DSL compiles per rank go from 1435 to 479 at TP8 and server bring-up after the weight load from 583 s to 260 s. Decode performance is unchanged: both builds compile and capture the same kernels for every graph they replay.

Two changes in `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/`:
- `cutedsl/oproj/prepared.py`: `compile_oproj` was `@cache`d on arguments some kernels never read (the producer does not read `nb` / `has_delta` / `front`; the consumer does not read `k` / `mla` / the exact batch, only its thread-group count), so ~93 layers compiled ~570 o-projection kernels per rank. Each kind (producer, consumer, fused) is now cached on what it reads.
- `runtime/decode.py`: the decode loop only runs while a CUDA graph is captured (`plan`), but the providers were also prepared for the fixed sizes 1-8, 16, 32 and 64 on top of the captured ones. Only the captured (verify-rounded) sizes up to the step cap are prepared now; `BATCHES` remains the fallback when no capture sizes are known.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes these files' compile or batch logic (searched "specialized decode compile", "compile_oproj", "captured sizes specialized", "Kimi K3 startup compile"). #68158 applies the captured-widths idea to the ROCm specialized decode only. Related: the compile caches in #65026 / #66623 (they cache compiles across restarts; this removes unneeded ones, so the two compose), and #68731, which is blocked on this startup cost.

## Claims

- Specialized-decode startup, weights loaded -> server up, 8x B300, Kimi-K3.1-Pro, `--max-num-seqs 64`: TP8 583 -> 260 s, TP8 + DCP8 675 -> 316 s (CuTe DSL compiles per rank 1435 -> 479 and 1553 -> 549). The remaining cost over the stock decode is ~2.6 min (TP8) and ~3.6 min (TP8 + DCP8).
- No decode regression: same captured graphs, the same compiled kernel keys for them (the patched build compiles a strict subset of the base build's keys), and median step time / output throughput within the noted bounds at concurrency 1-64 for TP8, TP8 + DCP8 and TP8 without a drafter.

## Validation

8x B300, `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro`, base `0bf9c07376` (this PR's parent) vs this PR `2409d9a93a`, each a fresh precompiled install of that commit. The branch has since been rebased onto current main; no commit in between touches `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/specialized_decode/` or its tests (the rebased commit has the same patch id). Server (TP8 + DCP8 adds `--decode-context-parallel-size 8 --dcp-comm-backend a2a --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1`; the no-drafter run drops the speculative config and `--use-replayssm`, and uses the default capture sizes):

```bash
vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro --trust-remote-code --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 --use-replayssm --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --attention-config '{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4"}' \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --language-model-only \
  --speculative-config '{"model":"Inferact/Kimi-K3.1-Pro-DSpark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"method":"dspark","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":4.05}' \
  --compilation-config '{"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,80,120,160,240,320]}' \
  --additional-config '{"decode_backend":"latency_specialized"}'
vllm bench serve --backend openai --dataset-name random --random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 512 --ignore-eos \
  --temperature 0 --max-concurrency C --num-prompts N --seed S   # (C, N, S) = (1, 8, 101), (8, 64, 108), (32, 128, 132), (64, 256, 164)
```

Synthetic acceptance pins the acceptance length (4.05 in every run), so throughput does not move with draft quality; each bench uses its own seed (no prefix-cache reuse between benches); servers ran base, PR, PR, base (one server each for the no-drafter pair). Pass bounds were fixed before the run: median ITL within 1% or within the base-vs-base gap, throughput no more than 3% lower.

commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Reduce encoder graph fallback staging and audio metadata overhead after #68831, while preserving compact cached output storage. Capture limits, including the default **5,120 encoder tokens**, remain unchanged.

## Motivation

The [review benchmarks](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/68831#issuecomment-7056172375) found that enabling encoder graphs could slow down batches outside the captured range. The manager still sorted/concatenated inputs and cloned outputs per item. Returning batch-backed eager views would reduce that cost but let one cached item retain an entire batch. Short clips can exceed the item limit well below 5K tokens.

This follows up the merged PR: bypass unnecessary staging, compact only outputs with excess backing storage, batch the required allocations/copy, and remove repeated frontend/attention metadata work. Triton audio attention recomputed identical window lengths in each of the 18/32 encoder layers; it now computes them once per forward, including each graph replay.

## Claims

- The Qwen3 audio mixin opts into an internal fast path for whole-batch eager fallback: preserve input order, skip graph selection/concatenation, reuse compact outputs and compact oversized backing storage with `torch._foreach_clone`. Its default `False` leaves other encoders on their existing sorting, staging and postprocessing policy.
- CPU integer/NumPy bookkeeping and batched CUDA padding reduce audio frontend launches. Equal chunks use one packed copy; CUDA batches of at least 32 varied chunks use a zero-sentinel gather. Smaller varied batches and non-CUDA devices retain sequence padding.
- NVIDIA Triton audio forwards reuse one window-length tensor across layers. The optional attention argument retains the existing recomputation when omitted. No new capture buffers or user-facing settings/default changes.

## Validation

Runtime validated at `0dd3188c12`; final head `3553b262bf` differs only in documentation, docstrings and tests (executable code unchanged); comparison base **main `dd8c157895`**. GB200, BF16, TRITON_ATTN, TP=1. Full public ASR-0.6B audio architecture (18×896) and Omni-30B-A3B audio architecture (32×1280), held seeded random weights and synthetic mel inputs. Model/batch token limits 8,192, max sequences 128, default auto graph budgets capped at **5,120**, auto item limit 78, 34 graphs.

| Model | All 30 cases vs main + graphs | 14 fallbacks vs main eager |
|---|---:|---:|
| ASR | 6.5–20.2% faster | 4.2–16.6% faster |
| OMNI | 4.8–15.4% faster | 4.0–12.7% faster |

These are **encoder-stage wall latencies**, including CNN, host metadata, sorting/staging/copies, transformer/projection, output handling and GPU completion. Feature extraction, decoder/serving queues, capture and JIT are outside the timed region. Each model's full run has 30 workloads, **72 samples per arm**, 12 warmups, three rotating inputs. One GPU workload runs at a time on GPU0 with CPUs 20–23. Each complete block contains all 24 permutations of four arms, shuffled and repeated three times, so every arm occupies every position equally. The fresh critical-case repeats add an identical main-eager arm as an ordering/noise control (largest observed median difference 0.50%).

| Workload | Tokens | ASR: main graphs / main eager → PR (ms) | Omni: main graphs / main eager → PR (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 short clips | 416 | 2.559 / 9.218 → 2.222 | 3.776 / 16.852 → 3.409 |
| One long clip | 1,664 | 4.726 / 9.658 → 4.001 | 6.639 / 15.892 → 5.876 |
| Long + 16 short clips | 1,768 | 5.044 / 9.908 → 4.274 | 7.105 / 15.976 → 6.281 |
| One clip near 5K | 4,992 | 11.711 / 11.703 → 9.929 | 16.431 / 17.632 → 14.551 |
| One clip above 5K | 5,200 | 12.345 / 12.207 → 10.384 | 17.634 / 17.317 → 15.109 |
| Mixed clips above 5K | 5,200 | 12.534 / 12.203 → 10.436 | 17.971 / 17.308 → 15.275 |
| 96 equal short clips | 1,248 | 11.048 / 9.747 → 9.207 | 17.459 / 16.086 → 15.224 |

| 128 short clips | 1,664 | 12.057 / 10.302 → 9.627 | 18.056 / 16.280 → 15.280 |

The baselines remain fixed main controls. **Within the patched version**, graph-enabled fallback remains up to **4.1% slower than graphs-disabled eager** because the graphs-disabled path returns batch-backed views while fallback compacts cache outputs. The table does not claim zero overhead when toggling the feature in the patched version.

The former small-regression cases and 128-item boundary were also rerun in fresh processes with **240 samples/arm**, two complete permutation blocks, at the same final source:

IQRs describe within-run spread; the two process runs are reported separately rather than presented as a confidence interval.

### Memory and output correctness

| Fallback | ASR main → PR extra peak (MiB) | Omni main → PR extra peak (MiB) |
|---|---:|---:|
| one_above_cap | 2953.21 → 2943.45 | 2953.21 → 2943.45 |
